Create one instance per availability zone, at the tenth address of the zone's default subnet:

AMI=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/canonical/ubuntu/server/24.04/stable/current/amd64/hvm/ebs-gp3/ami-id --query Parameter.Value --output text)
for z in a b c; do
  read SUBNET CIDR <<< "$(aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-1$z Name=default-for-az,Values=true --query 'Subnets[0].[SubnetId,CidrBlock]' --output text)"
  ip=${CIDR%.*}.10
  ID=$(aws ec2 run-instances --image-id $AMI --instance-type t3.medium --subnet-id $SUBNET --private-ip-address $ip \
    --security-group-ids $SG --iam-instance-profile Name=ella-core-ssm \
    --block-device-mappings 'DeviceName=/dev/sda1,Ebs={VolumeSize=20,VolumeType=gp3}' \
    --tag-specifications "ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=ella-core-$z}]" \
    --query 'Instances[0].InstanceId' --output text)
  echo "ella-core-$z $ID $ip ${CIDR%.*}.1"
done

The output lists each instance's name, ID, address and gateway, e.g.:

ella-core-a i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60001 172.31.0.10 172.31.0.1
ella-core-b i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60002 172.31.80.10 172.31.80.1
ella-core-c i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60003 172.31.16.10 172.31.16.1

The following steps use these example values.

Create one instance per zone, at 10.10.1.10, 10.10.1.11 and 10.10.1.12:

i=10
for z in 1 2 3; do
  az vm create $G -n ella-core-$z --zone $z --size Standard_D2as_v7 \
    --image Canonical:ubuntu-24_04-lts:server:latest --vnet-name ella-vnet --subnet ella \
    --private-ip-address 10.10.1.$i --public-ip-address "" --nsg "" \
    --admin-username azureuser --ssh-key-values ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
  i=$((i+1))
done

docs.title: 4. Install Ella Core
docs.text:
Google CloudAWSAzure

On each instance:

gcloud compute ssh ella-core-<z> --zone us-central1-<z> --tunnel-through-iap

Limit the size of packets sent to the radio, so they fit in the VPN tunnel:

sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens4:
      routes:
        - to: 192.168.1.50/32
          via: 10.128.0.1
          mtu: 1300
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml
sudo netplan apply

Install Ella Core:

sudo snap install ella-core

Replace /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml with the following, setting bind-address to the instance's address:

logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "ens4"
  n3:
    name: "ens4"
  n6:
    name: "ens4"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
cluster:
  bind-address: "10.128.0.10:7000"

Start Ella Core:

sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored

On each instance:

aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id>

Limit the size of packets sent to the radio, so they fit in the VPN tunnel. Set via to the instance's gateway from step 3, e.g. 172.31.0.1:

sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens5:
      routes:
        - to: 192.168.1.50/32
          via: 172.31.0.1
          mtu: 1300
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml
sudo netplan apply

Install Ella Core:

sudo snap install ella-core

Replace /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml with the following, setting bind-address to the instance's address from step 3:

logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "ens5"
  n3:
    name: "ens5"
  n6:
    name: "ens5"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
cluster:
  bind-address: "172.31.0.10:7000"

Start Ella Core:

sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored

On each instance:

az network bastion ssh $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-<z> --query id -o tsv) \
  --auth-type ssh-key --username azureuser --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

Limit the size of packets sent to the radio, so they fit in the VPN tunnel:

sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    eth0:
      routes:
        - to: 192.168.1.50/32
          via: 10.10.1.1
          mtu: 1300
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml
sudo netplan apply

Install Ella Core:

sudo snap install ella-core

Replace /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml with the following, setting bind-address to the instance's address:

logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "eth0"
  n3:
    name: "eth0"
  n6:
    name: "eth0"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
cluster:
  bind-address: "10.10.1.10:7000"

Start Ella Core:

sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored

docs.title: 5. Form the cluster
docs.text:
Google CloudAWSAzure

Open each node's UI through IAP, each in its own terminal:

gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel ella-core-a 5002 --local-host-port=localhost:5002 --zone us-central1-a
gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel ella-core-b 5002 --local-host-port=localhost:5003 --zone us-central1-b
gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel ella-core-c 5002 --local-host-port=localhost:5004 --zone us-central1-c
  1. Open https://localhost:5002 and initialize node a.
  2. Open Cluster, click Add Node, click Mint Token, and copy the token.
  3. Open https://localhost:5003, click Join an existing cluster instead, paste the token, enter 10.128.0.10:7000, and click Join.
  4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node c, at https://localhost:5004.

Open each node's UI through Session Manager, each in its own terminal:

aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id-a> --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSession --parameters portNumber=5002,localPortNumber=5002
aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id-b> --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSession --parameters portNumber=5002,localPortNumber=5003
aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id-c> --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSession --parameters portNumber=5002,localPortNumber=5004
  1. Open https://localhost:5002 and initialize node a.
  2. Open Cluster, click Add Node, click Mint Token, and copy the token.
  3. Open https://localhost:5003, click Join an existing cluster instead, paste the token, enter node a's address from step 3 with port 7000, e.g. 172.31.0.10:7000, and click Join.
  4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node c, at https://localhost:5004.

Open each node's UI through Bastion, each in its own terminal:

az network bastion tunnel $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-1 --query id -o tsv) --resource-port 5002 --port 5002
az network bastion tunnel $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-2 --query id -o tsv) --resource-port 5002 --port 5003
az network bastion tunnel $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-3 --query id -o tsv) --resource-port 5002 --port 5004
  1. Open https://localhost:5002 and initialize node 1.
  2. Open Cluster, click Add Node, click Mint Token, and copy the token.
  3. Open https://localhost:5003, click Join an existing cluster instead, paste the token, enter 10.10.1.10:7000, and click Join.
  4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node 3, at https://localhost:5004.

On the Cluster page, the three nodes appear as Healthy.

docs.title: 6. Configure the network
docs.text:
In the UI:

  1. In Operator, set the MCC, MNC and TAC to match the radio and SIM cards.
  2. In Data Networks, open internet and set its MTU to 1300.
  3. In Subscribers, add each SIM card.

docs.title: 7. Connect the radio
docs.text:
Give the radio a static address on the site network, e.g. 192.168.1.50/24 with gateway 192.168.1.1.

Configure an IPsec tunnel on the radio:

Google CloudAWSAzure Setting Value Peer The VPN gateway address ($GW) IKE version IKEv2 Authentication The pre-shared key in radio-vpn.psk Local ID The site's public address, e.g. 203.0.113.10 Remote ID The VPN gateway address Local subnet 192.168.1.50/32 Remote subnet 10.128.0.0/20 IKE and ESP AES-256, SHA-256, DH group 14 (MODP 2048) IKE lifetime 10 h or less IPsec SA lifetime 3 h or less

Set the radio's MME (4G) or AMF (5G) addresses to 10.128.0.10, 10.128.0.11 and 10.128.0.12, then restart the radio.

Setting Value Peer The tunnel's outside address ($GW) IKE version IKEv2 Authentication The pre-shared key in radio-vpn.psk Local ID The site's public address, e.g. 203.0.113.10 Remote ID The tunnel's outside address Local subnet 192.168.1.50/32 Remote subnet 172.31.0.0/16 IKE and ESP AES-256, SHA-256, DH group 14 (MODP 2048) IKE lifetime 8 h or less IPsec SA lifetime 1 h or less

Set the radio's MME (4G) or AMF (5G) addresses to the three instance addresses from step 3, e.g. 172.31.0.10, 172.31.80.10 and 172.31.16.10.

Setting Value Peer The VPN gateway address ($GW) IKE version IKEv2 Authentication The pre-shared key in radio-vpn.psk Local ID The site's public address, e.g. 203.0.113.10 Remote ID The VPN gateway address Local subnet 192.168.1.50/32 Remote subnet 10.10.0.0/16 IKE and ESP AES-256, SHA-256, DH group 14 (MODP 2048) IKE lifetime 8 h or less IPsec SA lifetime 7.5 h or less

Set the radio's MME (4G) or AMF (5G) addresses to 10.10.1.10, 10.10.1.11 and 10.10.1.12, then restart the radio.

docs.title: 8. Verify
docs.text:
Check that the tunnel is up:

Google CloudAWSAzure 
gcloud compute vpn-tunnels describe radio-tunnel $R --format='value(status)'

The output is ESTABLISHED.

aws ec2 describe-vpn-connections --vpn-connection-ids $VPN --query 'VpnConnections[0].VgwTelemetry[0].Status' --output text

The output is UP.

az network vpn-connection show $G -n radio-tunnel --query connectionStatus -o tsv

The output is Connected.

The radio appears on the Radios page, and attached phones appear as Registered on the Subscribers page.

docs.title: Enable MCPTT
docs.text: This guide shows how to serve Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) to subscribers over 4G and 5G, with an external IMS and an MCPTT server. To learn how Ella Core works with the IMS, see IMS Integration.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• IMS: an IMS integrated with Ella Core, as in Integrate with an IMS. Its P-CSCF must send the MCPTT ICSI, urn:urn-7:3gpp-service.ims.icsi.mcptt, in the AF-Application-Identifier of MCPTT calls.
  • MCPTT server: Ella IMS, set up as in Enable Push-to-Talk, or a 3GPP MCPTT server that the IMS reaches and trusts.
  • MCPTT clients: configured with the MC data network (mcx below) as their MC services APN or DNN.
  • Radios: support for QCI/5QI 69 and 65.
  • SIMs: with an ISIM you can program.
  • Phones: an IMS client that registers with a reg-id.

docs.title: 1. Create the MC data network
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to the Networking page and open the Data Networks tab.

Click Create, enter mcx as the Name, set an IP pool, turn on IMS (voice and mission critical services), and click Create.

Open the mcx data network, and in Slices, select the slice of your MCPTT users and click Serve on slice.

docs.title: 2. Create the MC profile
docs.text:
Go to the Profiles page and click Create. Enter a Name, e.g. mcptt, and click Create.

Click on the new profile, click Add Policy, and set:

  • Data Network: mcx.
  • 5QI / QCI: 69 — Mission critical signalling.
  • Allocation and Retention Priority (ARP): a level between 1 and 8, e.g. 3.
  • Pre-emption capability: May pre-empt.
  • Pre-emption vulnerability: Not pre-emptable.

Click Create.

Also add the policies the MCPTT users have on their current profile, e.g. on internet and ims.

docs.title: 3. Add the MCPTT application server
docs.text:
Go to Integrations › IMS. Under Application Servers, click Add Application Server, click Fill for Ella IMS MCPTT, and click Add.

With another MCPTT server, enter mcptt as the Name, its SIP URI as the Server Name, and an Identity matching its identities, e.g. sip:!.*!@mcptt.example.org.

docs.title: 4. Create the MCPTT service profile
docs.text: In Integrations › IMS, under Service Profiles, click Add Service Profile. Enter mcptt as the Name. Under Add from preset, select the MCPTT Preset and the mcptt Application Server, and click Add Criteria. Click Add.

docs.title: 5. Give the MC profile the MCPTT service profile
docs.text: Go to the Profiles page and click on the MC profile. Click the edit icon next to IMS Service Profiles, select mcptt for MCPTT and, for MMTel (voice, SMS), the service profile of the users' current profile, if any. Click Save.

docs.title: 6. Put MCPTT users on the MC profile
docs.text:
For each MCPTT user:

  • Go to the Subscribers page and click on the subscriber.
  • In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to Profile, select the MC profile, and click Update.
  • Give the subscriber an MSISDN, as in Enable Voice, and map its MCPTT public identity, sip:mcptt-<msisdn>@<IMS home domain>, to an MCPTT ID on your MCPTT server.
  • Program the SIM's ISIM with sip:mcptt-<msisdn>@<IMS home domain> in a record of EF.IMPU after the first.

docs.title: 7. Verify the MCPTT registration
docs.text: Start the MCPTT client. Go to the Subscribers page and click on the MCPTT user. MCPTT should show Registered.

docs.title: 8. Make an MCPTT call
docs.text:
On the MCPTT client, make a call to another MCPTT user. The call should connect with audio in both directions.

Enable MCPTT in Ella Core

docs.title: Enable SMS
docs.text: This guide connects Ella Core to an SMSC, such as Ella SMSC, so subscribers can send and receive SMS.

docs.title: 1. Configure the SMSC
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to Integrations › SMS. Under This Core, note the Diameter Realm, e.g. epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and each node's Origin-Host.

Set your SMSC's HSS realm to the Diameter Realm. If your SMSC asks for Ella Core's Origin-Host, enter each node's.

docs.title: 2. Connect Ella Core to the SMSC
docs.text:
In Integrations › SMS, click the edit icon next to Serving Node Number, enter Ella Core's E.164 number for SMS, e.g. +15550001111, and click Update.

Click Add SMSC and configure the following settings:

  • Name: a name for your SMSC, e.g. main.
  • Service Centre Addresses: the E.164 service centre addresses your SMSC serves, e.g. +15550000000.
  • Diameter Peers: the Address of your SMSC's Diameter endpoint. If your SMSC has several Diameter nodes, click Add Diameter Peer for each.

Click Add.

Validate that each node shows Connected.

docs.title: 3. Give subscribers an MSISDN
docs.text:
For each subscriber that should send or receive SMS:

  • Go to the Subscribers page and click on the subscriber you want to configure.
  • In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to MSISDN.
  • Enter the subscriber's E.164 number, e.g. +15551230001, and click on Update.

docs.title: 4. Set the SMSC number on the phones
docs.text: On each phone's SIM, set the SMSC number to one of your SMSCs' service centre numbers, in international format, e.g. +15550000000.

docs.title: 5. Send a test SMS
docs.text:
Send a test SMS message from a phone to another in your private mobile network. The message should be delivered successfully.

Enable SMS in Ella Core

To also deliver SMS over IP through an IMS, see Ella IMS's Enable SMS over IP.

docs.title: Enable UE-to-UE communication
docs.text: Local Switching allows two UEs served by Ella Core to communicate directly with each other.

docs.title: Enable local switching
docs.text:
1. Open the Ella Core UI and navigate to Networking > Data Networks, then open the data network of the UEs.
  2. In Slices, toggle Local switch to ON on the slice of the UEs.

Local switching only connects UEs on the same slice and data network.

The change takes effect on the user plane immediately.

Note

These steps can also be performed via the REST API. See the Slices API reference for details.

docs.title: Enable Voice
docs.text: This guide lets subscribers in your private mobile network make voice and video calls over 4G and 5G, with an external IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• IMS: an IMS integrated with Ella Core, as in Integrate with an IMS.
  • Radio QoS support: your radios must support the following QoS classes, as QCIs on 4G and 5QIs on 5G.
QCI / 5QI Used for 5 IMS signalling 1 Voice 2 Video

docs.title: 1. Create the voice data network
docs.text:
Go to the Networking page and open the Data Networks tab.

Click Create, enter ims as the Name, set the IP pool, turn on IMS (voice and mission critical services), and click Create.

Open the ims data network, and in Slices, select the slice of your subscribers and click Serve on slice.

docs.title: 2. Add a voice policy to the profiles
docs.text:
For each profile whose subscribers should make calls:

  • Go to the Profiles page and click on the profile you want to configure.
  • Click Add Policy, enter a Name, set the Data Network to ims, and click Create.

docs.title: 3. Give subscribers an MSISDN
docs.text:
For each subscriber that should make or receive calls:

  • Go to the Subscribers page and click on the subscriber you want to configure.
  • In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to MSISDN.
  • Enter the subscriber's E.164 number, e.g. +15551230001, and click on Update.

docs.title: 4. Enable voice on the phones
docs.text:
On each phone, turn on VoLTE (4G) or VoNR (5G).

In Integrations › IMS, check that Advertise IMS Voice is on, the default.

docs.title: 5. Verify the IMS registration
docs.text: Go to the Subscribers page and click on a subscriber with an MSISDN. Voice should show Registered.

docs.title: 6. Make a test call
docs.text:
Call a phone from another in your private mobile network. The call should connect with audio in both directions.

Enable Voice in Ella Core

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Ensure your system meets the requirements. Then, choose one of the installation methods below.

Snap (Recommended)SourceDockerKubernetes

Install the Ella Core snap:

sudo snap install ella-core

Configure Ella Core:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml

Start Ella Core:

sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored

Install the required dependencies:

sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc

Clone the Ella Core repository:

git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git
cd core

Build the frontend:

npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui

Build Ella Core:

REVISION=`git rev-parse HEAD`
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/ellanetworks/core/version.GitCommit=${REVISION}" ./cmd/core/main.go

Configure Ella Core:

vim core.yaml

Start Ella Core:

sudo ./main -config core.yaml

Create a new directory:

mkdir ella
cd ella

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
configs:
  ella_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        system:
          level: "info"
          output: "stdout"
        audit:
          output: "stdout"
      db:
        path: "/data/ella.db"
      interfaces:
        n2:
          address: "10.3.0.2"
          ngap-port: 38412
        n3:
          name: "n3"
        n6:
          name: "eth0"
        api:
          address: "0.0.0.0"
          port: 5002
      datapath:
        attach-mode: "tcx"

services:
  ella-core:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core:v1.22.0
    configs:
      - source: ella_config
        target: /core.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    entrypoint: /bin/core --config /core.yaml
    privileged: true
    volumes:
      - ella-data:/data
    ports:
      - "5002:5002"
    networks:
      default:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: eth0
      n3:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: n3
        ipv4_address: 10.3.0.2

networks:
  n3:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 10.3.0.0/24

volumes:
  ella-data:

Edit the file to match your network interfaces and desired configuration.

Note

This example uses tcx mode. To use xdp-native, run the container with network_mode: host and set n3 and n6 to host NICs with native XDP support.

Start the Ella Core container:

docker compose up -d

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the Multus CNI installed, and that the macvlan, static, and tuning CNI plugins are present on every node.

Download the Ella Core manifests:

git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.22.0 https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git

Edit core/k8s/core-ran-nad.yaml to set master to the host interface that connects to your radios, and set the N2/N3 address.

Deploy Ella Core:

kubectl apply -k core/k8s

Note

These manifests use tcx mode. To use xdp-native, move physical N3 and N6 NICs with native XDP support into the pod (e.g. with host-device) instead of using macvlan and eth0, and put both in a VRF.

docs.title: Integrate with an IMS
docs.text:
This guide connects Ella Core to an external IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS), with Ella Core as the IMS's HSS and PCRF. It is the first part of Enable Voice and Enable MCPTT. To learn how Ella Core works with the IMS, see IMS Integration.

This guide uses Ella IMS, but any 3GPP-compliant IMS can be used. For the Ella IMS side, see Integrate with Ella Core.

docs.title: 1. Enable the Diameter interface
docs.text:
In the Ella Core configuration file, set the address Ella Core accepts Diameter connections on:

interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.3.0.2"

In a high availability cluster, use the same interfaces.diameter.port on every node.

Restart Ella Core.

docs.title: 2. Configure the IMS
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to Integrations › IMS. Under This Core, note the Diameter Realm, e.g. epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, each node's Origin-Host, the Diameter Address, and the Home Domain.

Configure your IMS with the following settings:

  • HSS (Cx): Ella Core's Diameter Address, e.g. 10.3.0.2, port 3868.
  • PCRF (Rx): Ella Core's Diameter Address, e.g. 10.3.0.2, port 3868.
  • HSS and PCRF realm: Ella Core's Diameter Realm, or its Home Domain.
  • Home domain: Ella Core's Home Domain, e.g. ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org.

To use another home domain, e.g. ims.example.org, click the edit icon next to Home Domain, enter it, click Update, then Confirm. Set the same home domain on your subscribers' ISIMs.

docs.title: 3. Allow your IMS nodes
docs.text:
In Integrations › IMS, under Allowed IMS Peers, click Add Allowed Peer and enter:

  • Name: e.g. cscf.
  • Origin-Host of an IMS node, e.g. scscf.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, or the Realm of your IMS nodes, e.g. ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, or both.
  • Source Addresses: the IP addresses or CIDR prefixes your IMS nodes connect from, e.g. 10.3.0.0/24. At least one is required.

Click Add. Repeat for each group of IMS nodes: I-CSCF, S-CSCF, P-CSCF and application servers.

docs.title: 4. Restrict Diameter access to your IMS nodes
docs.text: In Integrations › IMS, under This Core, click the edit icon next to Restrict to Allowed Peers, turn it on, and click Update.

docs.title: 5. Set the P-CSCF addresses
docs.text: In Integrations › IMS, click the edit icon next to P-CSCF Addresses, enter your IMS's P-CSCF addresses or host names, e.g. 10.6.0.5, and click Update.

docs.title: 6. Route the IMS data networks
docs.text: In your IMS, add a route to the IP pools of your IMS data networks via Ella Core's N6 address, with an MTU of 1400, e.g. ip route add 10.0.0.0/8 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400.

docs.title: Integrate with a Radio
docs.text:
Radios are automatically added to Ella Core as they connect to the network as long as they are configured to use the same Operator information as Ella Core.

Follow this guide to integrate Ella Core with a radio. This guide assumes you have already deployed Ella Core.

docs.title: 1. Configure the Operator information
docs.text:
1. Open Ella Core in your web browser.
  2. Click on the Operator tab in the left-hand menu.
  3. Edit the Operator information:
    • MCC: The Mobile Country Code for the operator.
    • MNC: The Mobile Network Code for the operator.
    • Supported TACs: A list of supported Tracking Area Codes (TACs).

docs.title: 2. Configure the radio
docs.text:
In your radio's configuration, you will likely need to specify the following information to connect it with a mobile core network:

  • AMF / MME Address: The address of the N2 / S1-MME interface on Ella Core.
  • PLMN ID: The Public Land Mobile Network Identifier. This is a combination of the Mobile Country Code (MCC) and the Mobile Network Code (MNC). You can find this information in Ella Core under Operator and Operator ID.
  • TAC: The Tracking Area Code. You can find this information in Ella Core under Operator and Supported TACs.
  • SST (5G only): The Slice/Service Type. Identifies a network slice. You can find this information in Ella Core under Networking and Slices.
  • SD (5G only): The Slice Differentiator. Optionally differentiates slices sharing the same SST. You can find this information in Ella Core under Networking and Slices.

Note

Each radio has its own configuration interface. Consult the radio's documentation for specific instructions.

docs.title: Use native XDP with veth interfaces
docs.text:
When Ella Core's N3 or N6 interface is a veth pair and XDP is set to native mode, the peer side of the veth must have an XDP program attached, or traffic redirected out of that interface fails. This guide attaches a minimal one.

For an explanation of why this is needed, see XDP redirect on veth pairs.

docs.title: 1. Install prerequisites
docs.text:
Install the BPF toolchain needed to compile the XDP program:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y clang llvm libbpf-dev linux-headers-$(uname -r)

docs.title: 2. Create the zero entrypoint program
docs.text:
Create a file called zero_entrypoint.c with the following content:

#include <linux/bpf.h>
#include <bpf/bpf_helpers.h>

SEC("xdp")
int zero_entrypoint(struct xdp_md *ctx)
{
    return XDP_PASS;
}

char _license[] SEC("license") = "GPL";

docs.title: 3. Compile the program
docs.text: clang -O2 -g -Wall -target bpf -c zero_entrypoint.c -o zero_entrypoint.o

docs.title: 4. Attach the program to the peer veth
docs.text:
Attach the compiled program to the peer veth interface. If the peer is in a network namespace (e.g. n3ns), use ip netns exec:

sudo ip netns exec n3ns ip link set dev n3-ran-veth xdpgeneric off
sudo ip netns exec n3ns ip link set dev n3-ran-veth xdp obj zero_entrypoint.o sec xdp

If the peer is not in a namespace:

sudo ip link set dev <peer-veth-name> xdp obj zero_entrypoint.o sec xdp

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text:
Confirm the program is attached:

sudo ip netns exec n3ns ip link show n3-ran-veth

You should see prog/xdp in the output.

docs.title: 6. Configure Ella Core for native XDP
docs.text:
Set the attach mode to xdp-native in the Ella Core configuration file:

datapath:
  attach-mode: "xdp-native"

Restart Ella Core for the change to take effect.

docs.title: Tune Network Performance
docs.text: This guide describes the steps and settings required to tune network performance for Ella Core. It was written with 10Gbps NICs in mind. The exact values required will depend on the hardware used.

docs.title: Configure transmit queue length
docs.text:
Increase the transmit queue length to 10000 by adding the following line to /etc/udev/rules.d/60-ella-core.rules for each interfaces handling N3 or N6 traffic:

KERNEL=="enp4s0f0", RUN+="/sbin/ip link set %k txqueuelen 10000"

docs.title: Configure multiqueue
docs.text:
For all interfaces handling N3 or N6 traffic, configure multiple queues. The appropriate number of queues is the larger between the number of cores and the maximum number of queues supported by the NIC:

nic=enp4s0f0
nproc=$(nproc)
max_allowed=$(sudo ethtool -l $nic | grep Combined | awk '{ print $2 }' | sort -n | head -n 1)
if [ $nproc -ge $max_allowed ]; then
    echo $nproc
else
    echo $max_allowed
fi

Assuming the above script output was 16, add the following line to /etc/udev/rules.d/60-ella-core.rules:

KERNEL=="enp4s0f0", RUN+="/usr/sbin/ethtool -L %k combined 16"

docs.title: Increase the NIC ring buffer sizes
docs.text:
Find the maximum allowed ring buffer sizes allowed by your hardware:

sudo ethtool -g enp4s0f0

The output should be similar to this:

Ring parameters for enp4s0f0:
Pre-set maximums:
RX:         8192
RX Mini:        n/a
RX Jumbo:       n/a
TX:         8192
TX push buff len:   n/a
Current hardware settings:
RX:         512
RX Mini:        n/a
RX Jumbo:       n/a
TX:         512
RX Buf Len:     n/a
CQE Size:       n/a
TX Push:        off
RX Push:        off
TX push buff len:   n/a
TCP data split:     n/a

Add the following line to /etc/udev/rules.d/60-ella-core.rules, using the values from the Pre-set maximums section:

KERNEL=="enp4s0f0", RUN+="/usr/sbin/ethtool -G %k rx 8192 tx 8192"

docs.title: Tune maximum backlog in the receive queues
docs.text:
Increase the maximum backlog in receive queues by adding the following content to /etc/sysctl.d/99-ella-core.conf:

# increase the maximum backlog
net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 182757

docs.title: Apply the changes
docs.text:
The changes in this guide can be applied by either rebooting, or running the following commands:

sudo udevadm trigger
sudo sysctl --system

docs.title: Scale Up a High Availability Cluster
Scale Up a High Availability Cluster
docs.text: This guide walks through adding a node to an existing Ella Core high-availability cluster.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A running HA cluster deployed (see Deploy a High Availability Cluster).
  • A prepared host with Ella Core installed per the Install guide with cluster.bind-address set in the configuration file.

docs.title: Add a node
docs.text:
1. Open the Cluster page on any node in the cluster.
  2. Click Add Node, click Mint Token, and copy the token.
  3. Start Ella Core on the new host.
  4. Open the new node's UI in a browser. Click on Join an existing cluster instead, paste the token, enter the cluster address of a node already in the cluster, and click Join.
  5. On the Cluster page, verify the new node appears and is shown as Healthy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella Core installed with Install or Deploy a High Availability Cluster.
  • The target release is the next minor release after the running one.

docs.title: 1. Review the release notes
docs.text: Read the release notes of the target release. Apply any action listed under Breaking changes.

docs.title: 2. Back up
docs.text: Create a backup with Backup and Restore.

docs.title: 3. Upgrade
docs.text:
StandaloneHigh Availability SnapDockerKubernetes 
sudo snap refresh ella-core

In docker-compose.yaml, set the image tag to the target release:

image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core:<target-version>

Recreate the container:

docker compose up -d

Download the manifests of the target release:

git clone --depth 1 --branch <target-version> https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git core-<target-version>

Reapply your changes to core-<target-version>/k8s/core-ran-nad.yaml and core-<target-version>/k8s/core-configmap.yaml.

Apply the manifests:

kubectl apply -k core-<target-version>/k8s

Wait for the rollout to complete:

kubectl -n ella rollout status statefulset/ella-core

Upgrade the followers first and the leader last. Repeat these steps for each node:

  1. Open the Cluster page on any healthy node other than the one you are about to upgrade.
  2. Click Drain next to the node. Wait until its Drain State is drained.

  3. On that host, refresh the snap:

    sudo snap refresh ella-core

  4. On the Cluster page, wait for the node to return to Healthy.

  5. Click Resume next to the node. Wait until its Drain State is active.

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
StandaloneHigh Availability 
curl -k <ella-core-api-url>/api/v1/status

Confirm version is the target release and ready is true.

On the Cluster page, confirm:

  • Every node's Version is the target release.
  • Every node is Healthy and its Drain State is active.
  • Schema shows a single version.

docs.title: Roll back
docs.text:
StandaloneHigh Availability SnapDockerKubernetes

  1. Stop Ella Core:

    sudo snap stop --disable ella-core.cored

  2. Revert to the previous release:

    sudo snap revert ella-core

  3. Restore the backup with Offline Restore.

  1. In docker-compose.yaml, set the image tag back to the previous release.

  2. Stop the container:

    docker compose stop

  3. Delete the database from the data volume:

    docker run --rm -v <project>_ella-data:/data alpine sh -c 'rm -rf /data/ella.db /data/ella.db-wal /data/ella.db-shm /data/raft /data/cluster-tls'

  4. Copy the backup into the data volume as restore.bundle:

    docker compose cp backup.tar.gz ella-core:/data/restore.bundle

  5. Recreate the container:

    docker compose up -d

  1. Scale Ella Core down:

    kubectl -n ella scale statefulset/ella-core --replicas=0

  2. Start a pod that mounts the data volume:

    kubectl -n ella run restore --image=alpine --restart=Never \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"restore","image":"alpine","command":["sleep","3600"],"volumeMounts":[{"name":"data","mountPath":"/data"}]}],"volumes":[{"name":"data","persistentVolumeClaim":{"claimName":"data-ella-core-0"}}]}}'
kubectl -n ella wait --for=condition=Ready pod/restore

  3. Delete the database and copy the backup as restore.bundle:

    kubectl -n ella exec restore -- sh -c 'rm -rf /data/ella.db /data/ella.db-wal /data/ella.db-shm /data/raft /data/cluster-tls'
kubectl -n ella cp backup.tar.gz restore:/data/restore.bundle
kubectl -n ella delete pod restore

  4. Download the manifests of the previous release:

    git clone --depth 1 --branch <previous-version> https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git core-<previous-version>

  5. Reapply your changes to core-<previous-version>/k8s/core-ran-nad.yaml and core-<previous-version>/k8s/core-configmap.yaml.

  6. Apply the manifests:

    kubectl apply -k core-<previous-version>/k8s

  7. Scale Ella Core up:

    kubectl -n ella scale statefulset/ella-core --replicas=1

  1. On every node, stop Ella Core and revert to the previous release:

    sudo snap stop --disable ella-core.cored
sudo snap revert ella-core

  2. Restore the backup with Offline Restore.

docs.title: Use VLANs
docs.text:
Any interface used by Ella Core can be on a VLAN interface. First, configure the VLAN on the host system, then use the name of the VLAN interface in the configuration file:

logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    address: "10.3.0.2"
    ngap-port: 38412
  n3:
    name: "ens5.103"
  n6:
    name: "ens3.106"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "xdp-native"
telemetry:
  enabled: false

docs.title: Use VRFs
docs.text: Any interface used by Ella Core can be in a VRF.

docs.title: Use netplan to configure N3 and N6 in a user-plane VRF
docs.text:
Edit your netplan configuration:

network:
  vrfs:
    up-vrf:
      table: 1001
      interfaces:
        - enp4s0f0
        - enp4s0f1
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.6.0.1
          metric: 100
        # High metric unreachable route to prevent lookups in other tables
        - to: 0.0.0.0/0
          type: unreachable
          metric: 9000
  ethernets:
    enp2s0:
      addresses:
        - 10.1.0.10/24
      nameservers:
        addresses:
          - 1.1.1.1
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.1.0.1
    enp4s0f0:
      addresses:
        - 10.6.0.3/24
    enp4s0f1:
      addresses:
        - 10.3.0.3/24

  version: 2

N3 and N6 must share a VRF

The N3 and N6 interfaces must be assigned to the same VRF. Ella Core will refuse to start otherwise.

docs.title: Configure Ella Core
docs.text:
Use the interfaces directly in the configuration file:

interfaces:
  n2:
    address: "10.1.0.10"
  n3:
    name: "enp4s0f1"
  n6:
    name: "enp4s0f0"
  api:
    address: "10.1.0.10"
    port: 5002

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
This section provides detailed reference material for Ella Core, from configuration options to complete API documentation.

  • API
  • Configuration File
  • Production Hardening
  • Observability
  • Connectivity
  • Performance
  • System Requirements
  • Supported Mobile Equipment
  • 3GPP Compliance
  • Releases

docs.title: 3GPP Compliance
docs.text:
Ella Core implements 3GPP-standard interfaces for signalling.

Note

Open an enhancement proposal if you notice a 3GPP-compliance gap or require a new capability for a production deployment.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
Interface Transport Cx Diameter over SCTP or TCP N1 NAS, over N2 N2 NGAP over SCTP N3 GTP-U over UDP (IPv4 and IPv6) N6 IP N32 HTTP/2 over TLS Rx Diameter over SCTP or TCP S1-MME S1AP over SCTP S1-U GTP-U over UDP (IPv4 and IPv6) S6a Diameter over SCTP S6c Diameter over SCTP; over SCTP or TCP with the IMS SGd Diameter over SCTP; over SCTP or TCP with the IMS Sh Diameter over SCTP or TCP SGi IP

Ella Core is a single binary and does not expose internal 3GPP interfaces. See Architecture.

docs.title: Registration and mobility
docs.text:
• Registration. 4G: attach, detach, and normal and periodic tracking area update. 5G: initial, mobility, and periodic registration, and UE- and network-initiated deregistration.
  • Service request. An idle UE returns to connected mode to resume its session.
  • Paging. Ella Core pages an idle UE when downlink data arrives for it.
  • Handover. 4G: S1 handover, and X2 handover via the Path Switch procedure. 5G: Xn handover, and N2 handover between radios served by Ella Core.
  • 4G/5G interworking. A device moving between 4G and 5G keeps its IP address and its session.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
Ella Core carries IP data sessions for 4G and 5G subscribers.

  • Session management. 4G PDN connectivity and 5G PDU sessions: establishment, modification, and release, including network-requested procedures.
  • Session types. IPv4, IPv6, and IPv4v6.
  • QoS. A default QoS flow (5G) or default bearer (4G) per session, with the 5QI/QCI, ARP priority level, and pre-emption capability and vulnerability of the session's policy.
  • DSCP marking. The UPF sets the DSCP of the outer IP header of downlink GTP-U packets on N3/S1-U.
  • Dynamic PCC rules. GBR and non-GBR rules from the PCRF/PCF. A rule with the 5QI/QCI and ARP of the default QoS flow or bearer is carried on it; other rules get dedicated QoS flows (5G) or dedicated bearers (4G), up to 4 per session. A change of a rule's ARP modifies its QoS flow or bearer in place. The Subscribers API lists each session's QoS flows or bearers.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Procedures. Identity, authentication, and security mode control.
  • Authentication. EPS-AKA on 4G, 5G-AKA on 5G.
  • Subscriber identity concealment. SUCI with the null scheme, Profile A, and Profile B, on 5G.
  • Ciphering and integrity. The null, SNOW 3G, and AES algorithms: EEA0/1/2 and EIA0/1/2 on 4G, NEA0/1/2 and NIA0/1/2 on 5G.

docs.title: SMS
docs.text:
• SMS over NAS. 4G (SMS in MME) and 5G.
  • Mobile-originated and mobile-terminated SMS. Relayed to and from external SMSCs over SGd.
  • HSS for the SMSC. Send Routing Info for SM, Report SM Delivery Status, and Alert Service Centre over S6c.
  • HSS for the IP-SM-GW. IP-SM-GW registration by Sh-Update of SMS registration info. Send Routing Info for SM proxied to the registered IP-SM-GW over S6c.

docs.title: Voice and IMS services
docs.text:
• IMS voice and video. VoLTE on 4G and VoNR on 5G, with an external IMS. EPS fallback from 5G to 4G.
  • MCPTT. On-network MCPTT on 4G and 5G, with an external IMS and MCPTT server. QCI/5QI 69 for signalling, 65 for calls, and the Rx MCPTT priority feature.
  • HSS for the IMS. User authorization, server assignment, location info, multimedia authentication, registration termination, and push profile over Cx.
  • User profile. Two implicit registration sets per subscriber with an MSISDN (MMTel and MCPTT), a service profile with initial filter criteria per set, and distinct and wildcarded Public Service Identities per application server.
  • PCRF for the IMS. AA, re-auth, session termination, and abort session over Rx, with GBR QoS for voice, video, and MCPTT.

docs.title: Roaming
docs.text:
Ella Core is a visited network for subscribers of roaming partners, with local breakout. See Roaming.

  • SEPP. N32-c and N32-f with TLS security.
  • 5G. Authentication, registration, and subscription data with the home network, and Steering of Roaming.
  • 4G. S6a with the home HSS, directly or through a Diameter Edge Agent.
  • Local breakout. When the home subscription allows it.
  • 4G/5G interworking. For roamers of partners with both a 4G and a 5G agreement.

docs.title: Location (beta)
docs.text: Cell identity and E-CID positioning: LPPa on 4G, NRPPa on 5G. GNSS positioning in standalone mode: LPP on 4G and 5G. See the Location API.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No emergency services. Emergency sessions and emergency service requests are rejected.
  • No home-routed roaming. Ella Core supports inbound roaming with local breakout only.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
Ella is configured using a yaml formatted file.

Start Ella core with the --config flag to specify the path to the configuration file.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• logging (object): The logging configuration.
    • system (object): The system logging configuration.
      • level (string): The log level. Options are debug, info, warn, error, and fatal.
      • output (string): The output for the logs. Options are stdout and file.
      • path (string): The path to the log file. Only used if the output is set to file.
    • audit (object): The audit logging configuration.
      • output (string): The output for the logs. Options are stdout and file.
      • path (string): The path to the log file. Only used if the output is set to file.
  • db (object): The database configuration.
    • path (string): The path to the SQLite database file.
  • interfaces (object): The network interfaces configuration.
    • n2 (object): The configuration for the n2 interface (N2 in 5G, S1-MME in 4G). This is the SCTP control-plane interface towards radios.
      • name (string): The name of the network interface to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided). When set, the server binds to all IP addresses configured on this interface.
      • address (string): The IP address to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided). When set, the server binds to this specific address.
      • ngap-port (int, optional): The SCTP port for the 5G N2 / NGAP listener. Default 38412.
      • s1ap-port (int, optional): The SCTP port for the 4G S1-MME / S1AP listener. Default 36412.
      • port (int, optional): Deprecated alias for ngap-port. Cannot be set together with ngap-port.
    • n3 (object): The configuration for the n3 interface (N3 in 5G, S1-U in 4G). This is the user plane interface towards radios.
      • name (string): The name of the network interface (optional: either name or address must be provided).
      • address (string): The address to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided).
    • n6 (object): The configuration for the n6 interface (N6 in 5G, SGi in 4G). This interface should be connected to the internet. It carries the default network instance.
      • name (string): The name of the network interface.
    • network-instances (list, optional): Additional N6 network instances, each with its own interface. Sessions use the network instance set in the network_instance field of their slice and data network (see Slices).
      • name (string): The network instance name. default is reserved for interfaces.n6.
      • n6 (object): The N6 interface of the network instance.
        • name (string): The name of the network interface. It can be a VLAN or a veth, in any VRF, but not the n3 or n6 interface or the interface of another network instance. It must exist when Ella Core starts.
    • api (object): The configuration for the api interface.
      • name (string): The name of the network interface to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided). When set, the server listens on all addresses (0.0.0.0) but uses SO_BINDTODEVICE to restrict incoming traffic to this interface. Use this when you want to bind to a device without pinning to a specific IP address.
      • address (string): The IP address to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided). When set, the server binds to this specific address.
      • port (int): The port to listen on.
      • tls (object): The TLS configuration (optional).
        • cert (string): The path to the TLS certificate file (optional).
        • key (string): The path to the TLS key file (optional).
    • diameter (object, optional): The configuration for the Diameter interface.
      • name (string): The name of the network interface to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided).
      • address (string): The IP address to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided).
      • port (int, optional): The port to listen on. Default 3868.
    • n32 (object, optional): The configuration for the N32 interface, towards the SEPPs of roaming partners.
      • name (string): The name of the network interface to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided).
      • address (string): The IP address to listen on (optional: either name or address must be provided).
      • port (int, optional): The port to listen on. Default 443.
  • datapath (object): The datapath configuration (optional). When omitted, the datapath attaches at the XDP hook in driver mode where the network interface supports it, and at the TCX hook otherwise.
    • attach-mode (string): The kernel hook the datapath attaches to (optional): xdp-native, tcx, or xdp-generic. See the eBPF attach mode explanation.
  • xdp (object, deprecated): Replaced by datapath. Cannot be set together with datapath.
    • attach-mode (string): native is equivalent to datapath.attach-mode: xdp-native, generic to xdp-generic.
  • telemetry (object): The telemetry configuration.
    • enabled (boolean): Whether telemetry is enabled or not. Default is false.
    • otlp-endpoint (string): The endpoint for the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) collector.
  • cluster (object): Clustering configuration for high-availability deployments. See Clustering.
    • enabled (boolean): Enables HA mode. When false, Ella Core runs standalone.
    • node-id (int, 1–63, optional, deprecated): Node identity. Deprecated, the node ID is now generated automatically.
    • bind-address (string): host:port the cluster listener binds to. Carries Raft consensus and cluster HTTP over mTLS.
    • advertise-address (string, optional): host:port peers use to reach this node. Host may be an IP or DNS name. Defaults to bind-address.
    • peers (list of strings, optional, deprecated): host:port seed addresses. Deprecated, use the API or UI instead.
    • join-token (string, optional, deprecated): Single-use token minted on the cluster leader. Deprecated, use the API or UI instead.
    • initial-suffrage (string, optional, deprecated): voter or nonvoter. Defaults to voter. Deprecated, use the API or UI instead.
    • join-timeout (duration string, optional): How long a joining node keeps trying to reach a formed peer before it gives up and exits. Defaults to 2m.
    • propose-timeout (duration string, optional): Maximum wait for a Raft commit before the API returns 503.
    • snapshot-interval (duration string, optional): Minimum interval between automatic Raft snapshots.
    • snapshot-threshold (int, optional): Minimum number of applied log entries between automatic snapshots.
    • trailing-logs (int, optional): Number of Raft log entries retained after a snapshot, so a lagging follower can catch up by log replay instead of a full snapshot install. Defaults to the Raft library's default, currently 10240.

Note

When you use the Ella Core snap, the configuration file is located at /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml. After modifying the configuration file, restart Ella Core with sudo snap restart ella-core.cored for the changes to take effect.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "file"
    path: "/var/log/ella_system.log"
db:
  path: "/var/lib/ella-core/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    address: "22.22.22.2"
  n3:
    name: "ens5"
  n6:
    name: "ens3"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/etc/ella/cert.pem"
      key: "/etc/ella/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "xdp-native"
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  otlp-endpoint: "localhost:4317"

docs.title: Clustering
docs.text:
Enable clustering on each node to deploy Ella Core in a high-availability configuration. See Deploy a High Availability Cluster for the walkthrough.

cluster:
  bind-address: "10.0.0.1:7000"

docs.title: Connectivity
docs.text:
Ella Core uses 4 different interfaces by default:

Interface Role Transport name address Address families API The HTTP API and UI TCP, interfaces.api.port Yes Yes IPv4, IPv6 N2 / S1-MME Control plane between Ella Core and the radio SCTP, 38412 (5G) and 36412 (4G) by default Yes Yes IPv4, IPv6. N3 / S1-U User plane between Ella Core and the radio UDP 2152 Yes Yes IPv4, IPv6. N6 / SGi User plane between Ella Core and the internet. Additional N6 interfaces can be set in interfaces.network-instances. — Yes No Not configurable Cluster Raft consensus and cluster HTTP between Ella Core nodes, over mTLS, when clustering is enabled TCP, the port of cluster.bind-address No Yes IPv4, IPv6 SGd / S6c SMS between Ella Core and the SMSCs, when SMS is enabled SCTP, outbound to each SMSC node's port (3868 by default) No No IPv4, IPv6 Diameter Diameter from SMSC nodes, the IMS, including its IP-SM-GW, and roaming Diameter peers SCTP and TCP, interfaces.diameter.port (3868 by default). SMSC nodes and roaming peers over SCTP; IMS over SCTP or TCP. Yes Yes IPv4, IPv6 S6a 4G roaming between Ella Core and the HSS or Diameter Edge Agent of roaming partners SCTP, outbound to each roaming Diameter peer's port (3868 by default) No No IPv4, IPv6 N32 5G roaming between Ella Core and the SEPPs of roaming partners TCP, interfaces.n32.port (443 by default), inbound and outbound Yes Yes IPv4, IPv6 Connectivity in Ella Core

docs.title: Combining interfaces
docs.text: It is possible to combine interfaces in the following manners.

docs.title: Combined N2 and N3
docs.text:
Many radios can use a single network link towards the core. In this case, N2 and N3 can be combined by using the same interface name for both of them in the configuration file.

Combined N2 and N3

docs.title: Combined API and N6
docs.text:
The API interface is often the network interface with internet access, and the N6 interface also requires internet access. They can be combined by using the same interface name for both in the configuration file.

Combined API and N6

docs.title: Combined API/N6 and combined N2/N3
docs.text:
It is possible to use both combination together to reduce the requirements to 2 interfaces.

Combined All

One or both of these interfaces can be virtual interfaces, with veth. See Datapath constraints.

docs.title: Combined on one interface
docs.text: Ella Core can also be run with a single network interface. It can be achieved by using the same interface name in the configuration file, or by using VLANs.

docs.title: Using VLANs
docs.text: It is possible to use VLAN interfaces, with or without combining interfaces as described previously. In this case, the configuration file should contain the name of the VLAN interface, not the parent interface.

docs.title: Datapath constraints
docs.text:
The datapath attaches to N3 and every N6 interface at the hook set by datapath.attach-mode. The shape of those interfaces constrains which modes work.

  • veth, xdp-native: an XDP program must be attached to the peer interface, see the explanation and the setup guide.
  • veth, xdp-generic: TX checksum offload must be disabled on both ends (ethtool -K <veth> tx off), or decapsulated packets are silently corrupted.
  • veth, tcx or xdp-generic: segmentation offload must be disabled on the peer (ethtool -K <peer> tso off gso off), or the peer delivers merged packets that are dropped.
  • Any interface, tcx: Ella Core turns off GRO, hardware GRO and LRO on the interface before attaching. A feature that the driver or hypervisor fixes on stays on, and Ella Core logs a warning.
  • Any interface, xdp-generic: the kernel skips GRO and turns off hardware GRO and LRO on the interface while the program is attached.
  • macvlan or ipvlan, tcx or xdp-generic: packets are merged on the lower device, which Ella Core does not change. GRO, hardware GRO and LRO must be off on the lower device. Ella Core logs a warning at startup.
  • Merged packets: dropped, and counted in app_upf_datapath_drop_total with reason encap_gso or decap_gso.

docs.title: MTU
docs.text:
The MTU of a data network is the largest packet a subscriber sends or receives. On N3, each of these packets is carried in GTP-U (TS 29.281):

Header Size (bytes) Outer IPv4 / IPv6 20 / 40 UDP 8 GTP-U 8, plus 4 when the sequence number, N-PDU number or next extension header field is present, plus any extension headers

The data network MTU must not exceed the MTU of the path between the radio and Ella Core, minus the GTP-U overhead and the overhead of every tunnel on that path, such as IPsec.

N2 / S1-MME signalling crosses the same tunnels. When a tunnel drops larger packets without reporting its MTU, the route from Ella Core to the radios must have an MTU that fits the tunnel.

Setting Default Data network MTU 1400 Configuration The data network's page in the UI, or the Networking API

docs.title: NAT
docs.text: Property Behaviour Default Enabled on every slice and data network, except IMS data networks Address family IPv4 only Scope Per slice and data network. Uplink traffic leaving N6, sourced from the N6 address. Sessions on IMS data networks are never translated. Translated protocols TCP, UDP, and ICMP Source ports 1024-32767 Downlink traffic Delivered only when it matches a translation the subscriber's own traffic created. Untranslatable traffic IP fragments (nat_fragment) and protocols without ports, such as ESP and GRE (nat_unsupported_proto), are dropped. Protocols that embed addresses in their payload, such as FTP in active mode, do not work Configuration The Slices section of the data network's page in the UI, or the Slices API. Changes apply to established sessions and break their established connections.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Ella Core supports four observability pillars: Metrics, Logs, Traces, and Profiles.

docs.title: 1. Metrics
docs.text:
Ella Core exposes Prometheus metrics to monitor the health of an Ella Core instance.

Please refer to the metrics API documentation for more information on accessing metrics in Ella Core.

docs.title: Default Go metrics
docs.text: These metrics are used to monitor the health of the Go runtime and garbage collector. These metrics start with the go_ prefix.

docs.title: Custom metrics
docs.text:
These metrics are used to monitor the health of the system and the performance of your private network. These metrics start with the app_ prefix. The following custom metrics are exposed by Ella Core:

Metric Description Type app_connected_radios Number of radios currently connected to Ella Core, labeled by rat. Gauge app_signaling_messages_total Total radio signaling messages, labeled by rat, direction, and type. Counter app_registered_subscribers Number of subscribers currently registered in Ella Core, labeled by rat and roaming (true for roamers). Gauge app_registration_attempts_total Total UE registration (5G) and attach/tracking-area-update (4G) attempts, labeled by rat, type, result, and roaming (true for roamers). Counter app_sessions Number of active sessions currently in Ella Core, labeled by rat and roaming (true for roamers). Gauge app_session_establishment_attempts_total Total session establishment attempts, labeled by rat, result, and roaming (true for roamers). Counter app_session_releases_total Total session releases, labeled by rat and reason. Counter app_sms_attempts_total Total SMS attempts, labeled by direction (mo, mt) and result. Counter app_connected_service_centers Number of SMS service centers (SMSCs) connected to this node. Gauge app_connected_ims_nodes Number of IMS nodes connected to this node, which use it as their HSS or PCRF. Gauge app_diameter_rejected_peers_total Diameter peers whose capabilities exchange this node rejected, labeled by reason (not_allowed: the peer matches no allowed IMS peer while peers are restricted). Counter app_connected_roaming_partners Number of roaming partners connected to this node, labeled by interface: n32 (N32-c context established) or s6a (Diameter peer open). Gauge app_peer_requests_total Requests this node sent to the home network of roaming partners, labeled by interface (n32, s6a) and result (success, failure, error, timeout). Counter app_peer_request_duration_seconds Duration of requests this node sent to the home network of roaming partners, labeled by interface. Histogram app_ims_registered_subscribers Number of subscribers currently registered in IMS, across the cluster. Gauge app_ip_addresses_allocated The total number of IP addresses currently allocated to subscribers. Gauge app_ip_addresses The total number of IP addresses available for subscribers. Gauge app_upf_datapath_forward_total Packets the data plane forwarded, labeled by direction and action. Counter app_upf_datapath_drop_total Packets the data plane did not forward, labeled by direction and reason. Counter app_upf_datapath_fib_lookup_total FIB lookup outcomes in the data plane labeled by direction and result. Counter app_upf_bytes_total Total number of bytes transmitted through the data plane, labeled by direction. This value includes the Ethernet header. Counter app_upf_session_forwarded_packets_total Packets forwarded for sessions, labeled by direction, sst, sd, dnn, and fiveqi (QCI for 4G sessions). Counter app_upf_session_forwarded_bytes_total Bytes forwarded for sessions, labeled by direction, sst, sd, dnn, and fiveqi. This value excludes the tunnel and Ethernet headers. Counter app_upf_session_dropped_packets_total Packets dropped for sessions, labeled by direction, sst, sd, dnn, fiveqi, and reason. Counter app_upf_radio_forwarded_packets_total Packets forwarded for sessions, labeled by direction and radio_id. Counter app_upf_radio_forwarded_bytes_total Bytes forwarded for sessions, labeled by direction and radio_id. This value excludes the tunnel and Ethernet headers. Counter app_upf_radio_dropped_packets_total Packets dropped for sessions, labeled by direction, radio_id, and reason. Counter app_radio_info Radios known to this node or counted by its data plane, labeled by radio_id (global RAN node ID) and radio (name, empty when the radio is no longer registered). Always 1. Gauge app_upf_bpf_map_entries Entries currently installed in a data plane BPF map, labeled by map. Divide by app_upf_bpf_map_max_entries for a fill ratio. Gauge app_upf_bpf_map_max_entries Capacity of a data plane BPF map, labeled by map. Gauge app_upf_bpf_map_memory_bytes Kernel memory locked by a data plane BPF map, labeled by map. Gauge app_upf_nat_evictions_total Conntrack entries the data plane found evicted under load and re-created, labeled by the direction. Counter app_upf_dl_buffer_capture_attempts_total Downlink packets for an idle UE the data plane offered to the buffer, labeled by result. Counter app_upf_dl_buffer_evictions_total Buffered downlink packets discarded before re-injection, labeled by reason. Counter app_upf_ringbuf_events_lost_total Events the data plane raised but could not place in a ring buffer, labeled by map. Counter app_upf_usage_dropped_bytes_total Subscriber usage bytes the data plane measured but never recorded, labeled by reason (outcome_unknown, shutdown, stale_session, no_imsi). Counter app_upf_sessions_pending_cleanup Data plane sessions a failed operation left awaiting teardown, as of the last cleanup retry. Gauge app_api_requests_total Total number of HTTP requests by method, endpoint, and status code Counter app_api_request_duration_seconds HTTP request duration histogram in seconds Histogram app_api_authentication_attempts_total Total number of authentication attempts by type and result Counter app_database_storage_bytes The total storage used by the database in bytes. This is the size of the database file on disk. Gauge app_database_queries_total Database queries, labeled by table, operation, and error_type (empty on success and for results such as not found, already exists, or a conflict; otherwise the SQLite extended result code, an error class, or _OTHER). Counter app_database_query_duration_seconds Database query duration in seconds, labeled by table and operation. Histogram app_raft_changeset_bytes_total SQLite changeset bytes applied through the Raft FSM. Emitted only when clustering is enabled. Counter app_radio_events_dropped_total Radio events not written to the database because the write buffer was full. Counter

Note

When clustering is enabled, Ella Core also exports the full hashicorp/raft metrics suite (prefix raft_).

docs.title: 2. Logs
docs.text:
Ella Core produces three types of logs:

  • System Logs: General operational information about the system.
  • Audit Logs: Logs of user actions for security and compliance. You can view audit logs and manage their retention via the API and the Web UI.
  • Radio Logs: Logs related to NGAP (5G) and S1AP (4G) messages. You can view radio logs and manage their retention via the API and the Web UI.

All logs are output in JSON format with structured fields for easy parsing and ingestion into log aggregation systems like Loki, Elasticsearch, or Splunk.

For more information on configuring logging in Ella Core, refer to the Configuration File documentation.

Note

Ella Core does not assist with log rotation; we recommend using a log rotation tool to manage log files.

docs.title: 3. Traces
docs.text:
Ella Core supports distributed tracing using OpenTelemetry. Traces are exported via OTLP (gRPC) to any compatible backend such as Jaeger, Tempo, or Honeycomb.

Traces are collected for the following components:

  • NGAP/S1AP: Traces for NGAP (5G) and S1AP (4G) message handling between radios and Ella Core.
  • Diameter: Traces for Diameter requests sent and received, continued across peers.
  • API: Traces for HTTP requests to the REST API, except /api/v1/livez and /api/v1/readyz.
  • Cluster: Traces for requests forwarded between nodes in a high-availability deployment.
  • Database: Traces for database queries, following the OpenTelemetry database semantic conventions.

For more information on configuring tracing in Ella Core, refer to the Configuration File documentation.

docs.title: RAN Trace Correlation
docs.text:
When tracing is enabled, Ella Core sends each UE's 3GPP trace identifier to the radio in the NGAP or S1AP Trace Activation IE. A radio that uses this identifier for its own spans joins Ella Core's trace for the UE.

Item Value OpenTelemetry trace ID 8 octets 0x00 ‖ NG-RAN / E-UTRAN Trace ID (8 octets) Trace Collection Entity IP Address N2 interface address

docs.title: 4. Profiles
docs.text:
Ella Core exposes the http/pprof API for CPU and memory profiling analysis. This allows users to collect and analyze profiles of Ella Core using visualization tools like pprof or pyroscope.

For more information on accessing the pprof API in Ella Core, refer to the pprof API documentation.

docs.title: Alert Rules
docs.text: Ella Core ships with pre-configured Grafana alert rules that detect the most important failure scenarios.

docs.title: No Radios Connected
docs.text:
Critical. No radios connected for 2 minutes.

Check that the radio is powered on, reachable from the core, and configured with this core's address and PLMN.

docs.title: High Registration Failure Rate
docs.text:
Critical. More than 10% of registration attempts rejected over 5 minutes.

Break down app_registration_attempts_total by result, then check the subscriber's credentials, profile, and policy.

docs.title: High PDU Session Failure Rate
docs.text:
Critical. More than 10% of session establishments rejected over 5 minutes.

Break down app_session_establishment_attempts_total by result, then check the subscriber's policy, its data network, and the IP pool.

docs.title: IP Address Pool Near Exhaustion
docs.text:
Warning. More than 90% of the data network IP pool is allocated.

Enlarge the data network's IP pool, or remove subscribers that no longer need addresses. New PDU sessions fail once the pool is full.

docs.title: High Data Plane Packet Drop Rate
docs.text:
Warning. More than 10 packets/s dropped by the data plane for 5 minutes.

Break down app_upf_datapath_drop_total by reason and direction to localise the drop.

docs.title: No Data Plane Traffic
docs.text:
Critical. Radios connected but zero uplink and downlink throughput for 10 minutes.

Confirm a subscriber is actually sending traffic, then check the data network and route configuration.

docs.title: Data Plane Aborted Actions Detected
docs.text:
Critical. Any drop with an internal_ reason for 2 minutes.

An internal_ reason means Ella Core's data plane failed rather than dropping traffic by policy. Break down app_upf_datapath_drop_total by reason and report it.

docs.title: Flow Reports Being Dropped
docs.text:
Warning. Any flow report dropped in the last 5 minutes.

Data usage reporting is incomplete while this persists. Shorten the flow report retention policy, or report this if it continues at normal traffic levels.

docs.title: Data Plane Sessions Awaiting Cleanup
docs.text:
Warning. Data plane sessions have awaited teardown for 15 minutes.

A failed session operation left these sessions holding data plane resources, and Ella Core retries their teardown in the background. Check the logs for session cleanup retry failed, and report the error if it persists. Each one reduces the capacity left for new sessions.

docs.title: High API Error Rate
docs.text:
Warning. More than 5% of API responses are 5xx over 5 minutes.

Break down app_api_requests_total by endpoint and status to identify the failing endpoint.

docs.title: High API Latency (P99)
docs.text:
Warning. P99 API response time exceeds 2 seconds over 5 minutes.

Check database query latency and CPU usage on the Deep Dive dashboard.

docs.title: Authentication Failure Spike
docs.text:
Warning. More than 25% of API authentication attempts fail over 5 minutes.

Review the audit log to identify the source and whether the credentials are still valid.

docs.title: Instance Down
docs.text:
Critical. The scrape target is unreachable for more than 20% of the last 10 minutes.

Check that the Ella Core process is running and reachable from the metrics collector. Note that this only proves the collector can reach the core, not that radios can.

docs.title: High Memory Usage
docs.text:
Warning. Resident memory is forecast to exceed 1 GiB within 48 hours, based on the last 6 hours of growth, sustained for 30 minutes.

Compare heap profiles in Pyroscope to find what is retaining memory. Tune the 1 GiB ceiling to your deployment size, and the 48 hour horizon to how much warning you want.

docs.title: High Goroutine Count
docs.text:
Warning. Goroutine count is forecast to exceed 10,000 within 48 hours, based on the last hour of growth, sustained for 30 minutes.

This indicates a resource leak in Ella Core. Capture a goroutine profile from Pyroscope and report it.

docs.title: High Database Error Rate
docs.text:
Warning. More than 5% of database queries fail over 5 minutes, while the node runs more than one query per second. Raft leadership errors during an election do not count.

Break down app_database_queries_total by table, operation, and error_type to identify the failing queries.

docs.title: High Database Query Latency (P99)
docs.text:
Warning. P99 database query latency exceeds 500ms over 5 minutes.

Check the database size and the query rate on the Deep Dive dashboard.

docs.title: Large Database Size
docs.text:
Warning. Database file exceeds 1 GiB for 10 minutes.

Shorten the retention policy for network logs, audit logs, or flow reports.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: This reference document contains performance test results of Ella Core, covering data plane throughput, latency, and session support.

docs.title: Throughput (iPerf3)
docs.text:
The following table outlines the performance test results of Ella Core's data plane throughput:

Table 1. Data plane throughput (iPerf3)

Uplink (Gbps) Downlink (Gbps) 10+ 10+

The tests could saturate the 10Gbps connection consistently, with or without NAT enabled, with CPU usage peaking at 8%.

docs.title: Throughput (TRex)
docs.text:
The following table outlines Ella Core's data plane throughput in millions of packets per second (Mpps), in xdp-native and tcx modes, for subscriber IP packets of 46, 494 and 1456 bytes:

Table 2. Data plane throughput by attach mode and packet size (TRex)

Mode Direction Throughput (Mpps) 46 B 494 B 1456 B xdp-nativeUplink2.052.050.81 Uplink (NAT)1.721.700.81 Downlink3.152.170.81 tcxUplink0.880.880.81 Uplink (NAT)0.820.820.81 Downlink1.661.580.81

The packet size represents only the IP packet for the subscribers and ignores Ethernet and GTP encapsulation.

Downlink performance is higher because the flows can be handled by different cores using Receive Side Scaling (RSS). The uplink flows are all seen by the NIC drivers as the same flow, because of the GTP encapsulation.

Downlink with NAT was not supported by our testing script.

docs.text:
The following table outlines the performance test results of Ella Core's data plane latency:

Table 3. Data plane round-trip latency

Average (ms) Best (ms) Worst (ms) Mean Deviation (ms) 1.160 0.803 1.457 0.194

The value represents the round-trip-response times from the subscriber's device to the server and back.

docs.title: Session Support
docs.text: Ella Core can support up to 1000 subscribers using a data session simultaneously. This was tested with ueransim, using 10 simulated gNodeBs each handling 100 subscribers.

docs.title: Production Hardening
docs.text: This reference document provides guidelines for operating Ella Core in a production environment.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Deploy on a production-grade system. Ensure your system meets the production requirements.
  • Deploy with the snap: Use the Snap installation method to deploy Ella Core.
  • Isolate network interfaces: Use separate network interfaces for N2, N3, N6, and API traffic.
  • Secure roaming: Restrict N32 and S6a to your roaming partners, and use SEPP certificates issued by your CA.
  • Use TLS: Configure TLS for the API interface in the configuration file. Use certificates from a trusted Certificate Authority (CA).
  • Use the fastest attach mode the interfaces allow: set datapath.attach-mode to xdp-native where the driver supports it.
  • Set logging level to info: Configure system logging level to info.
  • Disable telemetry: Disable telemetry in the configuration file.
  • Back up the database: Back up the database file on a daily basis. Retain backups for at least 7 days.
  • Monitor metrics and logs: Operate an external Observability stack to collect and visualize metrics and logs exposed by Ella Core.

Ella Core runs on major Linux distributions including Ubuntu, Ubuntu Core, Debian, and Arch Linux (kernel 6.8 or later). It supports amd64 and arm64 architectures.

Minimum Production CPU 1 core 4 cores Memory 1 GB RAM 8 GB RAM Storage 10 GB disk space 50 GB disk space Network 1 interface with XDP support and appropriate MTU (see the official XDP documentation for driver support and the connectivity reference) 4 interfaces with XDP support and appropriate MTU (see the official XDP documentation for driver support and the connectivity reference) Operating System — Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Almost every operation requires a client token. The client token must be sent as Authorization HTTP Header using the Bearer scheme. That token can either be the JWT returned by the login endpoint or an API token.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Ella Core's API responses are JSON objects with the following structure:

{
  "result": "Result content",
  "error": "Error message",
}

Info

GET calls to the /metrics endpoint don't follow this rule, it returns text response in the Prometheus exposition format.

docs.title: OpenAPI Specification
docs.text:
The full API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella Core instance:

GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml  # Unauthenticated

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
• 200 - Success.
  • 201 - Created.
  • 400 - Bad request.
  • 401 - Unauthorized.
  • 429 - Too many requests.
  • 500 - Internal server error.

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
Ella Core provides a Go client for interacting with the API.

package main

import (
    "log"

    "github.com/ellanetworks/core/client"
)

func main() {
    clientConfig := &client.Config{
        BaseURL:  "http://127.0.0.1:5002",
        APIToken: "ellacore_Xl2yU1rcy2BP_8q5iOpNBtoXLYdwddbBCHInx",
    }

    ella, err := client.New(clientConfig)
    if err != nil {
        log.Println("Failed to create client:", err)
    }

    createSubscriberOpts := &client.CreateSubscriberOptions{
        Imsi:           "001010100000033",
        Key:            "5122250214c33e723a5dd523fc145fc0",
        SequenceNumber: "000000000022",
        ProfileName:    "default",
    }

    err = ella.CreateSubscriber(createSubscriberOpts)
    if err != nil {
        log.Println("Failed to create subscriber:", err)
    }
}

docs.title: Audit Logs
docs.text: In addition to system logs output, Ella Core exposes audit logs through its API.

docs.title: List Audit Logs
docs.text:
This path returns the list of audit logs.

Method Path GET /api/v1/logs/audit

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page. user query string — — Filter audit logs by user email. When omitted, all audit logs are returned. action query string — — Filter audit logs by action identifier (e.g. create_subscriber, auth_login). When omitted, all actions are returned. start query string — — Inclusive lower bound, RFC3339 (e.g. 2006-01-02T15:04:05Z). Unbounded when omitted. end query string — — Exclusive upper bound, RFC3339. Unbounded when omitted.

{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "1",

                "action": "create_user",

            }
        ],

}

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: This section describes the RESTful API for system user authentication.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
This path logs the user in and sets an httpOnly session cookie valid for 30 days.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/login

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• email (string): The email to authenticate with.

docs.title: Refresh
docs.text:
This path validates the current session cookie and returns a new JWT token. This token can then be used to authenticate future requests by sending it in the Authorization header using the Bearer <token> scheme. This token is valid for 15 minutes.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/refresh

Warning

Avoid relying on refresh tokens for API access since they require regular renewals. Instead, use API tokens which offer explicit expiry settings and can be manually revoked.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpZCI6MSwidXNlcm5hbWUiOiJhZG1pbiIsImV4cCI6MTczNTU4NTk0MX0.0BsZVMLCzJ6mzCXlf3qfAR2k6Fk7aUsGfHV7Tj1Dqy4"
    }
}

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/lookup-token

docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response

{
    "result": {
        "valid": true,
    }
}

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/rotate-secret

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Secret rotated successfully. All user sessions have been invalidated."

}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Flow Reports
docs.text: Flow reports provide visibility into network traffic patterns and usage statistics for subscribers. These reports are stored in the database and can be queried with various filters and pagination options.

docs.title: Get Flow Reports
docs.text:
This path returns a paginated list of flow reports with optional filtering.

Method Path GET /api/v1/flow-reports

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page. subscriber_id query string `` Filter by subscriber ID. protocol query int `` 1…255 Filter by protocol number. source query string `` Filter by source. Accepts: IP, IP:port, or :port. destination query string `` Filter by destination. Accepts: IP, IP:port, or :port. start query string now-7d Inclusive lower bound, RFC3339 (e.g. 2006-01-02T15:04:05Z). Matches flows overlapping the range. end query string now Exclusive upper bound, RFC3339. Matches flows overlapping the range. direction query string `` uplink, downlink Filter by traffic direction. action query string `` allow, drop Filter by flow action. allow returns only accepted flows, drop returns only dropped flows. When omitted, all flows are returned. group_by query string `` day, subscriber Grouping method for flow reports. When set, returns aggregated data instead of paginated list.

docs.text: The Integrations API provides endpoints to manage how Ella Core connects to external systems: SMS settings and SMSCs, IMS settings, allowed IMS peers, IMS application servers and service profiles, roaming (roaming partners, roaming Diameter peers, and the SEPP), and the Diameter status.
