docs.title: Get the IMS Settings
docs.text:
This path returns the P-CSCF addresses, the voice status, the IMS home domain, whether IMS voice is advertised, and whether peers are restricted to the allowed IMS peers.

Method Path GET /api/v1/integrations/ims

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "pcscfAddresses": ["192.0.2.20", "2001:db8::20"],
        "voiceStatus": "enabled",
        "homeDomain": "ims.example.org",
        "derivedHomeDomain": "ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "advertiseVoice": true,
        "restrictPeers": true
    }
}
Field Description voiceStatus Whether the IMS configuration is ready for voice: enabled, no_pcscf, no_ims_data_network (no IMS data network named ims), or ip_family_mismatch (no P-CSCF address shares an IP version with the pools of the ims data network). homeDomain The configured IMS home domain. Empty when derivedHomeDomain is used. advertiseVoice true when Ella Core tells home UEs that IMS voice is supported. restrictPeers true when only peers matching an allowed IMS peer may connect.

docs.title: Update the IMS Settings
docs.text:
This path sets the P-CSCF addresses, the IMS home domain, whether IMS voice is advertised, and whether peers are restricted to the allowed IMS peers. Changing the home domain moves the identities of the IMS application servers to the new domain and de-registers the subscribers whose public identities change.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/integrations/ims

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• pcscfAddresses (array of strings): Unicast IPv4 and IPv6 addresses or host names of the IMS, in preference order. At most 10, with at most 5 addresses of each IP version, without duplicates. UEs receive the addresses of the IP version they request. An empty list clears it. A changed list applies to new IMS sessions.
  • homeDomain (string): The IMS home domain, a domain name with at least two labels. An empty string, or the derived domain itself, uses the domain derived from the operator ID, ims.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org. The EPC realm and 3gppnetwork.org domains of other PLMNs are rejected. Ella Core accepts Diameter requests addressed to it.
  • advertiseVoice (boolean): Whether Ella Core tells every home UE that IMS voice is supported. It applies at each UE's next registration, attach or tracking area update. Roamers are never told.
  • restrictPeers (boolean): Whether only peers matching an allowed IMS peer may connect. With no allowed IMS peer, every peer is rejected. Turning it on disconnects connected peers that match none.

All four are required.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "pcscfAddresses": ["pcscf.ims.example.org", "192.0.2.20", "2001:db8::20"],
    "homeDomain": "ims.example.org",
    "advertiseVoice": true,
    "restrictPeers": true
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "IMS settings updated successfully"
    }
}

Method Path GET /api/v1/integrations/ims/allowed-peers

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "name": "cscf",
                "realm": "ims.example.org",
                "addresses": ["10.3.0.0/24", "2001:db8:3::/64"],
                "connections": [
                    {
                        "state": "open",
                        "originHost": "scscf.ims.example.org",
                        "realm": "ims.example.org",
                        "since": "2026-10-05T13:44:09Z"
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Get an Allowed IMS Peer
docs.text:
This path returns an allowed IMS peer.

Method Path GET /api/v1/integrations/ims/allowed-peers/{name}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Create an Allowed IMS Peer
docs.text:
This path creates an allowed IMS peer. At most 32 allowed IMS peers can be configured.

Method Path POST /api/v1/integrations/ims/allowed-peers

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the allowed IMS peer.
  • originHost (optional string): The Origin-Host the peer must give, a fully qualified domain name, compared case-insensitively.
  • realm (optional string): The Origin-Realm the peer must give, a fully qualified domain name.
  • addresses (array of strings): The IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or CIDR prefixes the peer connects from, at least one and at most 16, e.g. 10.3.0.5 or 10.3.0.0/24. A bare address means a /32 or /128 prefix. 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 allow any source address. They are returned as canonical prefixes, sorted and without duplicates.

At least one of originHost and realm is required.

A Diameter peer matches an allowed IMS peer when it connects from one of the addresses and gives the originHost and realm that are set. Matching peers are labelled ims. When restrictPeers is set in the IMS settings, other peers are rejected.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "name": "cscf",
    "realm": "ims.example.org",
    "addresses": ["10.3.0.0/24", "2001:db8:3::/64"]
}

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 201 Returns the created allowed IMS peer. 400 Invalid parameters. 409 The name is taken, or another allowed IMS peer has the same Origin-Host, realm and addresses.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "name": "cscf",
        "realm": "ims.example.org",
        "addresses": ["10.3.0.0/24", "2001:db8:3::/64"],
        "connections": []
    }
}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the application server.

  • publicServiceIdentities (optional array of strings): The SIP or tel URIs the application server hosts. A wildcarded identity uses the !regex! syntax, for example sip:!.*!@mcptt.ims.example.org. Identities are stored in canonical form: lowercase scheme and host, no URI parameters, and tel numbers without visual separators. An identity can't be hosted by, or overlap one of, another application server, be or cover a subscriber's public identity (sip:+<msisdn>@<IMS home domain>, tel:+<msisdn> or sip:mcptt-<msisdn>@<IMS home domain>), or take the form of a subscriber identity (sip:<IMSI>@<IMS home domain>).

docs.title: Get an IMS Service Profile
docs.text:
This path returns an IMS service profile.

Method Path GET /api/v1/integrations/ims/service-profiles/{name}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Create an IMS Service Profile
docs.text:
This path creates an IMS service profile.

Method Path POST /api/v1/integrations/ims/service-profiles

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the service profile.
  • initialFilterCriteria (optional array): In priority order (TS 29.228 Annex B.2.2). Each criterion has:
    • applicationServerName (string): The name of the IMS application server matching requests are sent to.
    • trigger (optional object): Without it, the criterion matches every request.
      • conditionsMatch (string): all if a group matches when all of its conditions match, and the trigger matches when any group matches. any if a group matches when any of its conditions matches, and the trigger matches when every group matches.
      • groups (array): Groups of conditions. Each condition has an optional negated (boolean) and exactly one of requestURI (string), method (string), sipHeader ({header, content}), sessionCase (ORIGINATING_REGISTERED, TERMINATING_REGISTERED, TERMINATING_UNREGISTERED, ORIGINATING_UNREGISTERED or ORIGINATING_CDIV) and sessionDescription ({line, content}). With the REGISTER method, registrationTypes lists up to two of INITIAL_REGISTRATION, RE-REGISTRATION and DE-REGISTRATION. Request URIs, headers, lines and contents are extended regular expressions.
    • profilePart (optional string): REGISTERED or UNREGISTERED, the part of the user profile the criterion belongs to. Omitted for both.
    • defaultHandling (optional string): SESSION_CONTINUED or SESSION_TERMINATED, what the S-CSCF does when the application server can't be reached.
    • serviceInfo (optional string): Passed transparently to the application server.
    • includeRegisterRequest (optional boolean)
    • includeRegisterResponse (optional boolean)

The priority of a criterion is its position in the list. It is returned on reads and ignored on writes.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "name": "conference",
    "initialFilterCriteria": [
        {
            "applicationServerName": "conference",
            "trigger": {
                "conditionsMatch": "all",
                "groups": [{"conditions": [{"requestURI": "^sip:conference@.*$"}]}]
            },
            "defaultHandling": "SESSION_TERMINATED"
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "name": "conference",
        "initialFilterCriteria": [
            {
                "priority": 0,
                "applicationServerName": "conference",
                "trigger": {
                    "conditionsMatch": "all",
                    "groups": [{"conditions": [{"requestURI": "^sip:conference@.*$"}]}]
                },
                "defaultHandling": "SESSION_TERMINATED",
                "includeRegisterRequest": false,
                "includeRegisterResponse": false
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: List Roaming Partners
docs.text:
This path returns the list of roaming partners. For a partner with a 5G agreement, n32 gives the N32-c context of this node, when it has interfaces.n32.

Method Path GET /api/v1/integrations/roaming/partners

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "0199a3c2-1f4e-7d21-8c9b-5a6e7f8091a2",
                "name": "Partner Telecom",
                "plmns": [
                    {"mcc": "999", "mnc": "70"}
                ],
                "profileName": "roamers",
                "sepp": {
                    "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org",
                    "n32cURI": "https://sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org:443",
                    "trustAnchorPEM": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
                },
                "diameterPeerID": "0199a3c2-5c1e-7b8e-9f3a-2d4c6e8f0a1b",
                "n32": {
                    "state": "established"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
N32 field Description state idle, establishing, established, failed, or unknown (the handshake could not start). peer The partner SEPP the context is with, when the handshake was redirected. lastError The reason of the last failure.

docs.title: Create a Roaming Partner
docs.text:
This path creates a new roaming partner.

Method Path POST /api/v1/integrations/roaming/partners

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the partner. Must be unique.
  • plmns (array): The partner's PLMN IDs, at least one.
    • mcc (string): 3 digits.
    • mnc (string): 2 or 3 digits.
    • nrfAPIRoot (string, optional): The apiRoot (http or https) of the NRF of this PLMN, for its roamers. Defaults to https://nrf.5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org of this PLMN ID. Needs sepp.
  • profileName (string): The name of the profile applied to the partner's roamers.
  • sepp (object, optional): The 5G agreement.
    • fqdn (string): The partner SEPP's FQDN, as in its certificate: <host>.5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org, or <host>.5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.<IPX ID>.ipxnetwork.org, for one of the partner's PLMN IDs.
    • n32cURI (string): The apiRoot of the partner SEPP's N32-c endpoint: https, host, optional port and optional path prefix.
    • n32fURI (string, optional): The apiRoot of the partner SEPP's N32-f endpoint. Defaults to n32cURI.
    • trustAnchorPEM (string): The CA certificates that the partner SEPP's certificate chains to, or the partner's self-signed certificate, in PEM. Each certificate must be valid, with an ECDSA key or an RSA key of at least 2048 bits.
  • diameterPeerID (string, optional): The ID of the roaming Diameter peer of the 4G agreement.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "name": "Partner Telecom",
    "plmns": [{"mcc": "999", "mnc": "70"}],
    "profileName": "roamers",
    "sepp": {
        "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org",
        "n32cURI": "https://sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org:443",
        "trustAnchorPEM": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
    },
    "diameterPeerID": "0199a3c2-5c1e-7b8e-9f3a-2d4c6e8f0a1b"
}

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 201 Returns the created partner. 400 Invalid parameters. 404 The profile or the roaming Diameter peer does not exist. 409 The name is taken, or a PLMN ID conflicts.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "id": "0199a3c2-1f4e-7d21-8c9b-5a6e7f8091a2",
        "name": "Partner Telecom",
        "plmns": [
            {"mcc": "999", "mnc": "70"}
        ],
        "profileName": "roamers",
        "sepp": {
            "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org",
            "n32cURI": "https://sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org:443",
            "trustAnchorPEM": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
        },
        "diameterPeerID": "0199a3c2-5c1e-7b8e-9f3a-2d4c6e8f0a1b"
    }
}

docs.title: Import a SEPP Certificate
docs.text:
This path replaces a node's SEPP certificate with one issued by your CA. When the FQDN or the trust anchor changes, the node runs the N32 handshake again with every partner.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/integrations/roaming/sepp/nodes/{seppID}/certificate

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• certificateChainPEM (string): The certificate, then any intermediates, ending with the CA certificate that partners trust. The certificate must be an end-entity certificate with keyUsage digitalSignature, extendedKeyUsage serverAuth and clientAuth (or none), and a subjectAltName DNS name under 5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org of your PLMN ID.
  • privateKeyPEM (string): The certificate's private key: ECDSA P-256 or P-384, or RSA of at least 2048 bits.
  • fqdn (string, optional): The node's SEPP FQDN, when the certificate has several DNS names. Defaults to the subject CN.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 200 Returns the imported certificate, as listed in Get the SEPP Status, with warnings: a missing extendedKeyUsage, a validity over 3 years, or a trust anchor that partners must import. 400 Invalid certificate or key. 409 Another node has this FQDN.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "seppID": 1,
        "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "source": "imported",
        "subject": "CN=sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "sans": ["sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
        "issuer": "CN=Operator Root CA",
        "notBefore": "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z",
        "notAfter": "2028-10-01T08:00:00Z",
        "fingerprint": "sha256:d4e5...01",
        "trustAnchorFingerprint": "sha256:77aa...3c",
        "warnings": [
            "The trust anchor of this node changed: every roaming partner must import the new trust anchor before N32 with this node works again"
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Delete a SEPP Certificate
docs.text:
This path deletes a node's SEPP certificate, generated or imported. The node then generates a new one signed by the cluster SEPP CA. Use it to return to a generated certificate after an import.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/integrations/roaming/sepp/nodes/{seppID}/certificate

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 200 The certificate was deleted. 400 seppID is not between 1 and 63. 404 The node has no SEPP certificate.

docs.title: Regenerate the SEPP CA
docs.text:
This path replaces the cluster SEPP CA and deletes every generated SEPP certificate; each node then generates a new one with the new CA. Imported certificates are kept.

Method Path POST /api/v1/integrations/roaming/sepp/ca/regenerate

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response

    "result": {
        "trustAnchor": {
            "source": "generated",
            "subject": "CN=SEPP CA,O=5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
            "fingerprint": "sha256:c47d...12",
            "notAfter": "2036-11-03T10:00:00Z",
            "pem": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n",
            "seppIDs": []
        },
        "warnings": [
            "The cluster SEPP CA changed: every roaming partner must import the new trust anchor before N32 with the nodes that use generated certificates works again"
        ]
    }
}

            "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",

docs.title: Location (beta)
docs.text:
Ella Core supports three positioning methods: Cell ID, Enhanced Cell ID (E-CID), and GNSS in standalone mode. The Location API requests a subscriber's location, manages periodic location requests, and provisions the cell positions those estimates are drawn from.

Beta

The Location API is experimental and served under /api/beta. Its paths and payloads may change without notice.

docs.title: Locate a Subscriber
docs.text:
This path returns a subscriber's current location.

Method Path POST /api/beta/location

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• supi (string): Subscriber identity.
  • method (string, optional): cell_id, ecid, or gnss. Defaults to cell_id.
  • mode (string, optional): network_based or ue_assisted for ecid; standalone for gnss. Defaults to every mode supported by method.
  • measurement_quantities (object, optional): E-CID measurement quantities (TS 38.455, TS 36.455). Only for ecid with mode network_based or omitted.
    • nr (array of strings, optional): Used when the serving cell is NR. Each entry must be one of cell-ID, sS-RSRP, sS-RSRQ, cSI-RSRP, cSI-RSRQ, angleOfArrivalNR, timingAdvanceNR, or uE-Rx-Tx-Time-Diff. No duplicates allowed.
    • eutra (array of strings, optional): Used when the serving cell is E-UTRA. Each entry must be one of cell-ID, angleOfArrival, timingAdvanceType1, timingAdvanceType2, rSRP, or rSRQ. No duplicates allowed.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 200 Returns a location estimate. 403 The subscriber is a roamer. 404 Subscriber not registered, or no estimate. 504 Location request timed out.

{

            }
        ],

            "plmnId": {
                "mcc": "001",
                "mnc": "01"
            },
            "nrCellId": "000000010"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Create a Deferred Location Request
docs.text:
This path starts periodic location reporting for a subscriber (TS 23.273 deferred location request).

Method Path POST /api/beta/location/deferred-requests

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• supi (string): Subscriber identity.
  • ldr_type (string): One of UE_AVAILABLE, PERIODIC, ENTERING_INTO_AREA, LEAVING_FROM_AREA, BEING_INSIDE_AREA, or MOTION. Only PERIODIC is supported.
  • periodic_event_info (object):
    • reporting_amount (integer): Number of reports, 1 to 8639999. Required unless reporting_infinite_ind is true.
    • reporting_interval (integer): Interval between reports in seconds, 1 to 8639999. reporting_amount x reporting_interval must not exceed 8639999.
    • reporting_infinite_ind (boolean, optional): Report until 8639999 seconds have elapsed.
    • reporting_interval_ms (integer, optional): 1 to 999. Not supported; reporting_interval is used.
  • scheduled_loc_time (string, optional): RFC 3339 time of the first report. Must be in the future.
  • method (string, optional): cell_id, ecid, or gnss. Defaults to cell_id.
  • mode (string, optional): network_based or ue_assisted for ecid; standalone for gnss. Defaults to every mode supported by method.
  • measurement_quantities (object, optional): As in Locate a Subscriber.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 201 Returns the deferred location request. 400 Invalid parameters. 403 The subscriber is a roamer. 404 Subscriber not registered on this node. 409 The subscriber already has an active deferred location request. 501 ldr_type is not supported. 503 Deferred location requests are unavailable.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
    "ldr_type": "PERIODIC",
    "periodic_event_info": {
        "reporting_amount": 120,
        "reporting_interval": 30
    },
    "method": "ecid",
    "mode": "network_based"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "id": "019a2f3c-8d1e-7b2a-9c4f-1e2d3c4b5a69",
        "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
        "ldr_type": "PERIODIC",
        "periodic_event_info": {
            "reporting_amount": 120,
            "reporting_interval": 30
        },
        "method": "ecid",
        "mode": "network_based",
        "status": "ACTIVE",
        "created_at": "2026-10-15T14:00:00Z"
    }
}

docs.title: List Deferred Location Requests
docs.text:
This path returns a paginated list of deferred location requests, newest first.

Method Path GET /api/beta/location/deferred-requests

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description supi query str Subscriber identity. status query str ACTIVE, TERMINATED Request status. page query int 1 >= 1 Page number. per_page query int 25 1..100 Items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description id string Request identifier. supi string Subscriber identity. ldr_type string PERIODIC. periodic_event_info object Accepted reporting parameters. scheduled_loc_time string Time of the first report. method string Positioning method. mode string Positioning mode. measurement_quantities object E-CID measurement quantities. status string ACTIVE or TERMINATED. termination_cause string NORMAL_TERMINATION, TERMINATION_BY_UE, or TERMINATION_BY_NETWORK (TS 29.572). termination_reason string ue_deregistered, ue_mobility, positioning_failed, node_restart, or node_shutdown. event_report_counter integer Number of reports produced (TS 29.572). Absent before the first report. created_at string Creation time. terminated_at string Termination time.

Terminated requests and their reports are deleted 7 days after termination. Each request keeps its 10000 most recent reports.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "019a2f3c-8d1e-7b2a-9c4f-1e2d3c4b5a69",
                "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
                "ldr_type": "PERIODIC",
                "periodic_event_info": {
                    "reporting_amount": 120,
                    "reporting_interval": 30
                },
                "method": "ecid",
                "mode": "network_based",
                "status": "TERMINATED",
                "termination_cause": "TERMINATION_BY_NETWORK",
                "termination_reason": "ue_deregistered",
                "event_report_counter": 42,
                "created_at": "2026-10-15T14:00:00Z",
                "terminated_at": "2026-10-15T14:21:03.512Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: List Location Reports

docs.title: Query Parameters

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description items[].seq integer Report number, starting at 1. items[].reported_at string Report time. items[].location_data object Location estimate, as returned by Locate a Subscriber. next integer Value to pass as after for the following reports.

docs.title: Create a Cell Position
docs.text:
This path provisions the geographic position of a cell antenna. Cell ID lookups resolve a subscriber's serving cell to this position.

Method Path POST /api/beta/cell-positions

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• rat (string): nr or eutra.
  • mcc (string): Mobile Country Code.
  • mnc (string): Mobile Network Code.
  • cell_identity (string): Hex cell identity (NCI for NR, ECI for E-UTRA).
  • gnb_id (string, optional): gNB identifier.
  • latitude (number): WGS-84 latitude in decimal degrees. Range -90…90.
  • longitude (number): WGS-84 longitude in decimal degrees. Range -180…180.
  • altitude (number, optional): Altitude, in metres.
  • uncertainty_semi_major (number, optional): Semi-major axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres.
  • uncertainty_semi_minor (number, optional): Semi-minor axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres.
  • orientation_major (integer, optional): Orientation of the semi-major axis, in degrees.
  • confidence (integer, optional): Confidence, in percent.

docs.text:
{
    "rat": "eutra",
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "cell_identity": "0000001",
    "latitude": 37.7749,
    "longitude": -122.4194
}

  • ipv6_pool (string, optional): The IPv6 pool of the data network in CIDR notation. Example: 2001:db8::/48.
  • dns (string): The IP address of the DNS server of the data network. Example: 8.8.8.8.
  • mtu (integer): The MTU of the data network. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
  • ims (boolean, optional): Whether this is an IMS data network. Defaults to true for a data network named ims, false otherwise. See IMS Integration.

  • dns (string): The IP address of the DNS server of the data network. Example: 8.8.8.8.
  • mtu (integer): The MTU of the data network. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
  • ims (boolean, optional): Whether this is an IMS data network. Enabling it requires every policy on the data network to use 5QI 5 or 69. Changing it releases the data network's sessions so that UEs reconnect. Omitted leaves it unchanged.

docs.title: Update BGP Settings
docs.text:
This path updates the BGP configuration. Enabling BGP starts the embedded BGP speaker. Changing the local AS or router ID triggers a restart of the speaker.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/networking/bgp

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• enabled (boolean): Enable or disable BGP.
  • localAS (integer): The local autonomous system number.
  • routerID (string): The BGP router ID, an IPv4 address. Leave it empty to adopt the N6 interface IPv4 address, which is then stored as the router ID. Enabling BGP with an empty router ID fails when the N6 interface has no IPv4 address.
  • listenAddress (string): The address and port to listen on (e.g. :179). An empty or unspecified address (:179, 0.0.0.0:179) accepts sessions on every address of this node; any other address must be one configured on this node and restricts the speaker to it. Outgoing connections to peers are not affected.

docs.text:

  • description (string): An optional description for the peer.
  • importPrefixes (array): List of prefix entries to accept from this peer. Each entry has prefix (CIDR string) and maxLength (integer). Use [{"prefix": "0.0.0.0/0", "maxLength": 32}] to accept all routes. Omit or set to [] to accept no routes.

docs.title: Update the Operator ID
docs.text:
This path updates the operator ID. The Mobile Country Code (MCC) and Mobile Network Code (MNC) are used to identify the operator. The operator ID can't be changed when there are subscribers created in the system. Changing it renames the Diameter identity and realm of every node, so the Ella Core peers configured in the IMS and in the SMSC must be updated afterwards. When no IMS home domain is configured, IMS application servers in the old IMS home domain move to the new one.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/operator/id

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• mcc (string): The Mobile Country Code (MCC) of the network. Must be a 3-digit string.
  • mnc (string): The Mobile Network Code (MNC) of the network. Must be a 2 or 3-digit string.

docs.title: Update the NAS Security Algorithms
docs.text:
This path updates the NAS security algorithm preference order for ciphering and integrity protection. The order determines which algorithms the network prefers during subscriber device security capability negotiation. Changes take effect for the next subscriber registration.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/operator/nas-security

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• ciphering (array of strings): The preferred ciphering algorithm order. Each entry must be one of NULL, SNOW3G, or AES. At least one algorithm is required, maximum 3. No duplicates allowed.
  • integrity (array of strings): The preferred integrity algorithm order. Each entry must be one of NULL, SNOW3G, or AES. At least one algorithm is required, maximum 3. No duplicates allowed.

These algorithm names are RAT-neutral: Ella Core signals them as NEA/NIA to 5G subscribers and as EEA/EIA to 4G subscribers.

Name 5G 4G NULL NEA0 / NIA0 EEA0 / EIA0 SNOW3G 128-NEA1 / 128-NIA1 128-EEA1 / 128-EIA1 AES 128-NEA2 / 128-NIA2 128-EEA2 / 128-EIA2

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "ciphering": ["AES", "SNOW3G"],
    "integrity": ["AES", "SNOW3G"]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Operator NAS security algorithms updated successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Create a Policy
docs.text:
This path creates a new policy. Optionally, you can create network rules as part of the policy.

Method Path POST /api/v1/policies

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The Name of the policy.
  • profile_name (string): The name of the profile associated with this policy. Must be the name of an existing profile.
  • slice_name (string): The name of the slice associated with this policy. Must be the name of an existing slice that serves the data network (see Slices).
  • session_ambr_uplink (string): Maximum uplink bitrate for a single PDU session (Session AMBR). Enforced by Ella Core. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "100 Mbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps.
  • session_ambr_downlink (string): Maximum downlink bitrate for a single PDU session (Session AMBR). Enforced by Ella Core. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "200 Mbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps.
  • var5qi (integer): 5G QoS Identifier (5QI). Signaled to the radio, which uses it for scheduling (latency budget, error rate, priority); on a 4G radio it is signaled as the equivalent QCI. Valid values: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 69, 70, 79, 80 (non-GBR only). Must be 5, or 69 for mission critical services, on an IMS data network.
  • arp (integer): Allocation and Retention Priority (1–15). Used by the radio at session setup for admission control and pre-emption decisions. Has no effect on traffic once the session is established. 1 = highest priority.
  • preemption_capability (string, optional): Whether the session's default bearer or QoS flow may pre-empt others at admission (TS 23.501 §5.7.2.2): may_preempt or not_preempt. Defaults to not_preempt. Must be not_preempt when arp is 15.
  • preemption_vulnerability (string, optional): Whether the session's default bearer or QoS flow may be pre-empted: preemptable or not_preemptable. Defaults to not_preemptable. Must be not_preemptable when arp is 15.
  • data_network_name (string): The name of the data network associated with the policy. Must be the name of an existing data network.
  • default (boolean, optional): Make this the profile's default APN/DNN binding (used for the 4G default bearer and 5G fallback). The first policy created in a profile becomes the default regardless.
  • rules (object, optional): Network rules to create with the policy, organized by direction. Rules are created in the order provided.

docs.title: Rules Object Structure
docs.text:
The rules object contains: - uplink (array, optional): Array of uplink rules - downlink (array, optional): Array of downlink rules

Each rule contains: - description (string): Description of the rule - remote_prefix (string, optional): IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR notation for remote prefix (e.g., "10.0.0.0/24" or "2001:db8::/32") or null. When omitted, matches any IP. - protocol (integer): Protocol number (0-255) - port_low (integer): Low port number (0-65535) - port_high (integer): High port number (0-65535) - action (string): "allow" or "deny"

docs.title: Update a Policy
docs.text:
This path updates an existing policy. Network rules are always replaced on every update call.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/policies/{name}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• profile_name (string): The name of the profile associated with this policy. Must be the name of an existing profile.
  • slice_name (string): The name of the slice associated with this policy. Must be the name of an existing slice that serves the data network (see Slices).
  • session_ambr_uplink (string): Maximum uplink bitrate for a single PDU session (Session AMBR). Enforced by Ella Core. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "100 Mbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps. The ceiling depends on the access the policy's profile permits: when 5G is allowed the number must not exceed 65535 in the chosen unit (TS 24.501 §9.11.4.14); when 4G is allowed the rate must not exceed 10 Gbps (TS 24.008 §10.5.6.5B).
  • session_ambr_downlink (string): Maximum downlink bitrate for a single PDU session (Session AMBR). Enforced by Ella Core. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "200 Mbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps. The ceiling depends on the access the policy's profile permits: when 5G is allowed the number must not exceed 65535 in the chosen unit (TS 24.501 §9.11.4.14); when 4G is allowed the rate must not exceed 10 Gbps (TS 24.008 §10.5.6.5B).
  • var5qi (integer): 5G QoS Identifier (5QI). Signaled to the radio, which uses it for scheduling (latency budget, error rate, priority); on a 4G radio it is signaled as the equivalent QCI. Valid values: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 69, 70, 79, 80 (non-GBR only). Must be 5, or 69 for mission critical services, on an IMS data network.
  • arp (integer): Allocation and Retention Priority (1–15). Used by the radio at session setup for admission control and pre-emption decisions. Has no effect on traffic once the session is established. 1 = highest priority.
  • preemption_capability (string, optional): may_preempt or not_preempt. Omitted leaves it unchanged. Must be not_preempt when arp is 15.
  • preemption_vulnerability (string, optional): preemptable or not_preemptable. Omitted leaves it unchanged. Must be not_preemptable when arp is 15.
  • data_network_name (string): The name of the data network associated with the policy. Must be the name of an existing data network.
  • default (boolean, optional): Make this the profile's default APN/DNN binding, clearing the previous default. Omitted or false leaves it unchanged.
  • rules (object, optional): Network rules to set on the policy. Existing rules are always deleted first. If this field is omitted, all existing rules are deleted.

docs.title: Rules Behavior
docs.text:
• Omit rules field: all existing rules are deleted.
  • Provide rules with arrays: existing rules are deleted and replaced with the new ones.
  • Provide empty arrays: all existing rules are deleted and no new rules are created.

To keep existing rules, you must re-supply them in every update request.

docs.title: Sample Request to Update Rules
docs.text:
{
    "session_ambr_uplink": "100 Mbps",
    "session_ambr_downlink": "200 Mbps",
    "var5qi": 9,
    "arp": 1,
    "data_network_name": "internet",
    "rules": {
        "uplink": [
            {
                "description": "Allow SSH",
                "protocol": 6,
                "port_low": 22,
                "port_high": 22,
                "action": "allow"
            },
            {
                "description": "Deny all",
                "protocol": 0,
                "port_low": 0,
                "port_high": 0,
                "remote_prefix": "0.0.0.0/0",
                "action": "deny"
            }
        ],
        "downlink": []
    }
}

docs.title: Sample Request to Delete All Rules
docs.text:
Omit the rules field (or provide empty arrays) to delete all existing rules:

{
    "session_ambr_uplink": "100 Mbps",
    "session_ambr_downlink": "200 Mbps",
    "var5qi": 9,
    "arp": 1,
    "data_network_name": "internet"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Policy updated successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Pprof
docs.text: Ella Core exposes a pprof compatible API for profiling analysis. Profiling endpoints are only available to admin users and scraping requires an API token.

docs.title: Profiling Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/v1/pprof/ An HTML page listing the available profiles. GET /api/v1/pprof/allocs A sampling of historical memory allocations over the life of the program. GET /api/v1/pprof/block A sampling of stack traces that blocked on synchronization primitives. GET /api/v1/pprof/cmdline The command line invocation of the program. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutine A stack trace of all current goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/heap A sampling of memory allocations of live objects. GET /api/v1/pprof/mutex A sampling of stack traces of holders of contended mutexes. GET /api/v1/pprof/profile A 30-second CPU profile. GET /api/v1/pprof/threadcreate A sampling of thread creation events. GET /api/v1/pprof/trace A 1-second execution trace. POST /api/v1/pprof/symbol Symbol information for program counter (PC) addresses, used by pprof tooling to map raw addresses back to function names.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Profiles define the subscriber's Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate (UE-AMBR) and the IMS service profiles of its registration sets. Ella Core signals the UE-AMBR to the radio, which enforces it. A profile groups the policies of its subscribers.

docs.title: List Profiles
docs.text:
This path returns the list of profiles.

Method Path GET /api/v1/profiles

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "name": "enterprise",
                "ue_ambr_uplink": "1 Gbps",
                "ue_ambr_downlink": "1 Gbps",
                "allow_4g": true,
                "allow_5g": true
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 10,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Create a Profile
docs.text:
This path creates a new profile.

Method Path POST /api/v1/profiles

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the profile.
  • ue_ambr_uplink (string): Aggregate uplink bitrate cap across all of the subscriber's sessions (UE-AMBR). Enforced by the radio. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "500 Mbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps.
  • ue_ambr_downlink (string): Aggregate downlink bitrate cap across all of the subscriber's sessions (UE-AMBR). Enforced by the radio. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "1 Gbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps.
  • allow_4g (boolean, optional): Whether subscribers using this profile may attach over 4G (EPC). Defaults to true.
  • allow_5g (boolean, optional): Whether subscribers using this profile may register over 5G (5GC). Defaults to true.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Profile created successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Update a Profile
docs.text:
This path updates an existing profile.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/profiles/{name}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• ue_ambr_uplink (string): Aggregate uplink bitrate cap across all of the subscriber's sessions (UE-AMBR). Enforced by the radio. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "500 Mbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps. The ceiling depends on the access the profile permits: 10 Gbps when 4G is allowed (S1AP BitRate, TS 36.413), otherwise 4 Tbps (NGAP BitRate, TS 38.413).
  • ue_ambr_downlink (string): Aggregate downlink bitrate cap across all of the subscriber's sessions (UE-AMBR). Enforced by the radio. Format: <number> <unit> (e.g. "1 Gbps"). Allowed units: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps. The ceiling depends on the access the profile permits: 10 Gbps when 4G is allowed (S1AP BitRate, TS 36.413), otherwise 4 Tbps (NGAP BitRate, TS 38.413).
  • allow_4g (boolean, optional): Whether subscribers using this profile may attach over 4G (EPC). Defaults to true.
  • allow_5g (boolean, optional): Whether subscribers using this profile may register over 5G (5GC). Defaults to true.

docs.title: Sample Response

{
    "result": {
        "message": "Profile updated successfully"

docs.title: Radios
docs.text:
Radios are automatically added to Ella Core after a successfull connection.

The Radio API provides endpoints to view information about radios and to forget offline ones.

docs.title: List Radios
docs.text:
This path returns the list of radios in the inventory.

Method Path GET /api/v1/ran/radios

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page. status query str online, offline Filter by presence status.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Radio name. ref string Radio identity, and the path segment that addresses it. Empty on a radio that has not completed setup. id string Radio identifier. plmn object The PLMN the radio belongs to. bit_length int Bit length of the gNB ID (22–32). Present on gNBs only. address string Radio address. On an offline radio, the last known address. type string Radio type: gNB, ng-eNB, eNB, N3IWF, or Unknown. status string online if the radio is currently associated with this node, offline otherwise. connected_at string When the radio associated (RFC 3339). On an offline radio, when it last associated. last_seen_at string Timestamp of the last message received from the radio (RFC 3339). disconnected_at string When the radio's association dropped (RFC 3339). Empty while the radio is online.

docs.title: Get a Radio
docs.text:
This path returns the details of a specific radio, connected or offline, including connection timestamps, RAN node type, and supported tracking areas. To list subscribers connected to this radio, use GET /api/v1/subscribers?radio={name}.

Method Path GET /api/v1/ran/radios/{ref}

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description ref string Radio identity, as returned in a radio's ref field: {type}:{mcc}-{mnc}:{id}, the id carrying @{bitLength} for a gNB. For example gNB:001-01:00002a@24 or eNB:001-01:MacroeNB-00008.

docs.title: Forget a Radio
docs.text:
This path drops an offline radio from the inventory.

Requires the admin role.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/ran/radios/{ref}

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description ref string Radio identity, as returned in a radio's ref field: {type}:{mcc}-{mnc}:{id}, the id carrying @{bitLength} for a gNB. For example gNB:001-01:00002a@24 or eNB:001-01:MacroeNB-00008.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 The radio was forgotten. 404 No offline radio carries that identifier. 409 The radio is online.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Radio forgotten successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: List Radio Events

docs.title: Roamers
docs.text: This section describes the RESTful API for managing roamers: subscribers of a roaming partner registered on the private mobile network.

docs.title: List Roamers
docs.text:
This path returns the list of roamers, ordered by IMSI.

Method Path GET /api/v1/roamers

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page. partner query str Filter by roaming partner name. radio query str Filter by radio name. data_network query str Filter by data network name, through the roaming partner's profile. search query str ≤ 254 chars Filter by IMSI or MSISDN substring.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 200 Returns the roamers. 400 Invalid parameters. 404 The roaming partner, radio or data network does not exist.

{

docs.title: Slices
docs.text: Each slice defines a Slice Service Type (SST) and an optional Slice Differentiator (SD). Ella Core uses slice information alongside the data network name to determine which policies apply to a subscriber's session.

docs.title: List Slices
docs.text:
This path returns the list of slices.

Method Path GET /api/v1/slices

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "name": "default",
                "sst": 1,
                "sd": "010203"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 10,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Create a Slice
docs.text:
This path creates a new slice.

Method Path POST /api/v1/slices

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the slice.
  • sst (integer): The Slice Service Type (SST). Must be an integer between 1 and 255.
  • sd (optional string): The Service Differentiator (SD). Must be a 3-byte hexadecimal string without the "0x" prefix. Ex. "010203".

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Slice created successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Get a Slice
docs.text:

Method Path GET /api/v1/slices/{name}

docs.title: Parameters

This path updates an existing slice.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/slices/{name}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• sst (integer): The Slice Service Type (SST). Must be an integer between 1 and 255.
  • sd (optional string): The Service Differentiator (SD). Must be a 3-byte hexadecimal string without the "0x" prefix. Ex. "010203".

    "result": {

This path deletes a slice from Ella Core. A slice cannot be deleted if it is referenced by any policy.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/slices/{name}

docs.title: Parameters

docs.title: List the Data Networks of a Slice
docs.text:
This path returns the data networks a slice serves, with the forwarding of each. A policy can only use a data network on a slice that serves it.

Method Path GET /api/v1/slices/{name}/data-networks

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "data_network": "internet",
                "nat": true,
                "local_switch": false,
                "network_instance": "default"
            }
        ]
    }
}
  • nat (boolean): Whether Ella Core translates the IPv4 addresses of the subscribers of this data network on this slice to the N6 address of the node that serves the session.
  • local_switch (boolean): Whether traffic between two subscribers of this data network on this slice is switched inside the user plane.
  • network_instance (string): The N6 network instance of the sessions: default, or a name from interfaces.network-instances.

docs.title: Serve a Data Network on a Slice
docs.text: Method Path POST /api/v1/slices/{name}/data-networks

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• data_network (string): The name of the data network.
  • nat (boolean, optional): Defaults to true, or false when the data network has framed routes. Always false on an IMS data network, and cannot be true while the data network has framed routes.
  • local_switch (boolean, optional): Defaults to false. Always true on an IMS data network.
  • network_instance (string, optional): Defaults to default.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "The slice now serves the data network"
    }
}

docs.title: Get a Data Network of a Slice
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/slices/{name}/data-networks/{data_network}

docs.title: Sample Response

        "nat": true,
        "local_switch": false,
        "network_instance": "default"
    }
}

docs.title: Update a Data Network of a Slice
docs.text:
Changes apply to established sessions without releasing them, except on a node that does not define the new network instance, which releases them. Changing nat breaks the established connections of the sessions.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/slices/{name}/data-networks/{data_network}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• nat (boolean, optional): Cannot be enabled on an IMS data network, or while the data network has framed routes. Omitted leaves it unchanged.
  • local_switch (boolean, optional): Cannot be disabled on an IMS data network. Omitted leaves it unchanged.
  • network_instance (string, optional): Empty means default. Omitted leaves it unchanged.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Slice data network updated successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Get the status
docs.text:
This path returns the status of Ella core.

Method Path GET /api/v1/status

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Response Headers
docs.text: When clustering is enabled, the response includes an X-Ella-Role header with the Raft role of the responding node (Leader, Follower, Candidate, Shutdown, or Unknown). Load balancers can use this header to direct write traffic to the leader.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "version": "v1.22.0",
        "revision": "388ce92244a0b304e9f6c15e3f896acee6fe7b1a",
        "initialized": true,
        "ready": true,
        "schemaVersion": 9,
        "datapathAttachMode": "xdp-native",
        "cluster": {
            "enabled": false,
            "nodeId": "0199c4f1-2a7e-7b31-9c5d-1f2e3a4b5c6d"
        }
    }
}

When clustering is enabled, the response includes a cluster object:

{
    "result": {
        "version": "v1.22.0",
        "revision": "388ce92244a0b304e9f6c15e3f896acee6fe7b1a",
        "initialized": true,
        "ready": true,
        "schemaVersion": 9,
        "datapathAttachMode": "xdp-native",
        "cluster": {
            "enabled": true,
            "role": "Leader",
            "nodeId": 1,
            "isLeader": true,
            "leaderNodeId": 1,
            "appliedIndex": 42,
            "clusterId": "my-cluster",
            "leaderAPIAddress": "https://10.0.0.1:5002"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Check Liveness
docs.text:
This path answers while the process serves HTTP. It takes no token.

Method Path GET /api/v1/livez

It answers 204 No Content.

docs.title: Check Readiness
docs.text:
This path returns whether the node is ready to receive traffic, and the result of each check. It takes no token.

Method Path GET /api/v1/readyz

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description cluster boolean Add the cluster check. Default false.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Name Passes when shutdown The node is not stopping. member The node finished starting and, in a cluster, joined it. initialized Clustering is disabled, or a user exists. drain Clustering is disabled, or the node is not draining or drained. database The database answers. leader The node leads, or heard from the leader within twice the election timeout. cluster Clustering is disabled, or the node leads and the cluster is healthy. Only with cluster=true.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description ready boolean Whether every check passes. checks array The checks, in order. checks[].name string Name of the check. checks[].ok boolean Whether it passes. checks[].detail string Why it fails. Empty when it passes.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 Every check passes. 400 cluster is not true or false. 503 A check fails.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "ready": false,
        "checks": [
            {"name": "shutdown", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "member", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "initialized", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "drain", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "database", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "leader", "ok": false, "detail": "no contact with the cluster leader for 12s"}
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Subscribers
docs.text: This section describes the RESTful API for managing network subscribers. Network subscribers are the devices that connect to the private mobile network.

docs.title: List Subscribers
docs.text:
This path returns the list of network subscribers, ordered by IMSI.

Method Path GET /api/v1/subscribers

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page. radio query str Filter by radio name. data_network query str Filter by data network name. search query str ≤ 254 chars Filter by IMSI, MSISDN or description substring.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "imsi": "001010100007487",
                "profile_name": "default",
                "description": "Warehouse gate reader",
                "msisdn": "+15551230001",
                "status": {
                    "registered": true,
                    "connection_state": "connected",
                    "systems": ["5G"],
                    "num_sessions": 1,
                    "last_seen_at": "2026-03-16T12:34:56Z",
                    "last_seen_radio": "gNB-1"

        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 10,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

description and msisdn are omitted from an item when unset.

docs.title: Create a Subscriber
docs.text:
This path creates a new network subscriber.

Method Path POST /api/v1/subscribers

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• imsi (string): The IMSI of the subscriber. Must be a 15-digit string starting with <mcc><mnc>.
  • key (string): The key of the subscriber. Must be a 32-character hexadecimal string.
  • sequenceNumber (string): The sequence number of the subscriber. Must be a 6-byte hexadecimal string.
  • profile_name (string): The profile name of the subscriber. Must be the name of an existing profile.
  • opc (optional string): The operator code of the subscriber. If not provided, it will be generated automatically using the Operator Code (OP) and the key parameter.
  • description (optional string): A free-text note about the subscriber. At most 64 characters.
  • msisdn (optional string): The subscriber's phone number in E.164 format, for example +15551230001. Unique across subscribers. Required for SMS.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Subscriber created successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Update a Subscriber
docs.text:
This path updates an existing network subscriber.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/subscribers/{imsi}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• profile_name (string): The profile name of the subscriber.
  • description (optional string): A free-text note about the subscriber. At most 64 characters. This path replaces the subscriber in full, so omitting the field clears the stored note.
  • msisdn (optional string): The subscriber's phone number in E.164 format, for example +15551230001. Unique across subscribers. This path replaces the subscriber in full, so omitting the field clears the stored MSISDN.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Subscriber updated successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Registrations
docs.text:
registrations holds one entry per mobility-management context. It is empty for a subscriber the core has never served.

Field Description system 5G or 4G. The core that registered the device. registered RM state in 5G, EMM state in 4G. false on an entry the core remembers but holds no context for. connection_state connected, idle, or null. CM state in 5G, ECM state in 4G. radio Radio serving this registration, or the last one that did when the device is idle or deregistered. last_seen_at Timestamp of last activity in this system (RFC 3339). imei 15-digit IMEI of the device. Absent once the core has released the context. ciphering_algorithm NEA0 / 128-NEA1..3 in 5G, EEA0 / 128-EEA1..3 in 4G. Absent when none is established. integrity_algorithm NIA0 / 128-NIA1..3 in 5G, EIA0 / 128-EIA1..3 in 4G. Absent when none is established. ims_voice_over_ps IMS voice over PS session indicator sent to the device in the registration accept (5G) or attach and tracking area update accept (4G). Absent once the core has released the context. connection UE-associated logical connection, or null when the device holds none.

docs.title: Connection identifiers
docs.text:
connection carries only the identifier pair belonging to the registration's system.

Field System Description amf_ue_ngap_id 5G AMF UE NGAP ID, INTEGER (0..2^40-1). Allocated by the core. ran_ue_ngap_id 5G RAN UE NGAP ID, INTEGER (0..2^32-1). Allocated by the serving radio. Absent until the radio allocates one, for example on a handover target before it accepts the handover. mme_ue_s1ap_id 4G MME UE S1AP ID, INTEGER (0..2^32-1). Allocated by the core. enb_ue_s1ap_id 4G eNB UE S1AP ID, INTEGER (0..2^24-1). Allocated by the serving radio. Absent until the radio allocates one.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: Field Description system 5G or 4G, matching a registration's system. id PDU Session ID (5G) or linked EPS Bearer ID (4G). status Session status (for example active, inactive). ip_type IPv4, IPv6 or IPv4v6. data_network DNN (5G) or APN (4G). slice S-NSSAI. 5G only. bearers The session's QoS flows (5G) or EPS bearers (4G), the default one first. Omitted when the core holds no session context.

docs.title: Bearers
docs.text: Field Description id QFI (5G) or EPS Bearer ID (4G). default true for the session's default QoS flow or bearer. var5qi 5QI (5G) or QCI (4G). arp ARP priority level, 1 (highest) to 15. preemption_capability may_preempt or not_preempt. preemption_vulnerability preemptable or not_preemptable. mbr_uplink, mbr_downlink Maximum bitrate. Present on GBR QoS flows and bearers. gbr_uplink, gbr_downlink Guaranteed bitrate. Present on GBR QoS flows and bearers. rules IDs of the PCC rules the QoS flow or bearer carries, such as those of an IMS call.

docs.title: IMS
docs.text: Field Description private_identity IMS private identity (IMPI): <imsi>@<IMS home domain>. scscf_name S-CSCF serving the subscriber. Absent when the subscriber is not registered in IMS. public_identities IMS public identities (IMPU): sip:+<msisdn>@<IMS home domain> and tel:+<msisdn> when the subscriber has an MSISDN, sip:mcptt-<msisdn>@<IMS home domain> when it also has an MCPTT service profile, and sip:<imsi>@<IMS home domain>, which is barred, also in the derived home domain when another IMS home domain is configured. public_identities[].identity The public identity. public_identities[].barred true when the identity cannot be used for calls. public_identities[].registration_set mmtel or mcptt. public_identities[].user_state The state of the identity's registration set: registered, registered_unreg_services, authentication_pending or not_registered.

docs.title: IP-SM-GW
docs.text:
The IP-SM-GW that registered for the subscriber. While it is registered, Ella Core sends the SMSC's routing requests for the subscriber to it.

Field Description number IP-SM-GW number in E.164 format. diameter_host Diameter identity of the IP-SM-GW. diameter_realm Diameter realm of the IP-SM-GW.

docs.title: Deregister a Subscriber from IMS
docs.text:
This path clears a subscriber's IMS registration and its registered IP-SM-GW. Ella Core asks the S-CSCF to deregister the subscriber, which ends the subscriber's calls, and the phone registers again. Ella Core clears its own state even if the S-CSCF does not answer, so use this path to recover when the IMS stopped without deregistering the subscriber.

Method Path POST /api/v1/subscribers/{imsi}/ims/deregister

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "IMS registration cleared",
        "acknowledged": true
    }
}

acknowledged is false when the S-CSCF did not answer. The S-CSCF may then still consider the subscriber registered.

docs.title: Generate Support Bundle
docs.text: Method Path POST /api/v1/support-bundle

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Property Value Status 200 Content-Type application/gzip Content-Disposition attachment; filename="ella-support-<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.tar.gz" Body gzipped tar archive

Warning

Support bundles contain operational data and personally identifiable information (PII). They should only be shared with trusted partners.

docs.title: Archive contents
docs.text:
Each member is best-effort: a collector that fails writes an error file in its place, and the request still returns 200.

Path Contents db.json Database export: bundle_metadata, operator, home_network_keys, policies, networking, subscribers, ip_leases, ims_application_servers, ims_service_profiles, ims_service_profile_assignments, radio_logs and other operational sections. The audit_logs section requires audit_logs:list; usage_per_day and usage_per_subscriber require subscriber_usage:get. Restricted sections are omitted and marked in bundle_metadata.sections. config.yaml Runtime configuration file logs/system.log Recent in-memory system logs, preserving original messages and identities collection_status.json Status of optional configuration, live UE and BPF collectors; database section status is recorded in db.json under bundle_metadata.sections amf_ues.json Live AMF and SMF UE state mme_ues.json Live MME UE state system/ Version, OS release, kernel, memory, CPU, disk and network diagnostics bpf/ eBPF map entries as gzipped NDJSON, with a _metadata.json index

docs.title: Redacted fields
docs.text:
Field Value in the bundle operator.OperatorCode * home_network_keys[].PrivateKey * bgp_peers[].password * subscribers[] imsi, msisdn and profile_id only; keys, OPc and sequence numbers are not exported cluster.join-token (config.yaml) * Live UE security state Curated exports omit authentication vectors and key material Application authentication data Password hashes, API/session token hashes, signing secrets and cluster authentication keys are not exported radio_logs[] Raw signaling payloads are excluded because they can contain security keys; event metadata and stored details are retained

System log retention is limited to 100,000 entries and 16 MiB of payload. An entry larger than 64 KiB is replaced with a valid JSON omission marker containing its original byte count. Its original message and fields are not retained in the bundle log buffer.

docs.title: Get Subscriber Usage

Absent returns both. limit query integer 1000 1–1000 With group_by=subscriber only: the maximum number of subscribers returned, ordered by total usage, highest first.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: This section describes the RESTful API for managing system users. System users are used to authenticate with Ella Core and manage the system.

docs.title: List Users
docs.text:
This path returns the list of system users.

Method Path GET /api/v1/users

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "email": "admin@ellanetworks.com",
                "role_id": 1
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 10,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Create a User
docs.text:
This path creates a new system user.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• email (string): The email of the user.
  • password (string): The password of the user.
  • role_id (int): The role ID of the user. Allowed values:
    • 1 (admin): Administrator user with full access to network and system resources.
    • 2 (read only): Read-only user with only read access to network resources.
    • 3 (network manager): Network manager user with full access to network resources.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User created successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Update a User
docs.text:
This path updates an existing system user.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• role_id (int): The role of the user. Allowed values:
    • 1 (admin): Administrator user with full access to network and system resources.
    • 2 (read only): Read-only user with only read access to network resources.
    • 3 (network manager): Network manager user with full access to network resources.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User updated successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Get a User
docs.text:
This path returns the details of a specific system user.

Method Path GET /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "email": "admin@ellanetworks.com",
        "role_id": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Delete a User
docs.text:
This path deletes a user from Ella Core.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User deleted successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Update My Password
docs.text:
This path updates the password of the currently authenticated user. After a successful password change, all existing sessions for the user are invalidated.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/me/password

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• current_password (string): The user's current password.
  • password (string): The new password.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User password updated successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Update a User Password
docs.text:
This path updates the password of a specific system user. After a successful password change, all existing sessions for the target user are invalidated. This path requires admin privileges.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}/password

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • password (string): The new password of the user.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User password updated successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Create an API Token
docs.text:
This path creates a new API token for the authenticated user. The token has the same permissions as your user account, and actions performed with it are logged under your user account. Maximum 12 tokens per user.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the API token (3–50 characters).
  • expires_at (string, optional): The expiration date of the API token in RFC 3339 format. If not provided, the token will never expire.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellacore_Xl2yU1rcy2BP_8q5iOpNBtoXLYdwddbBCHInx"
    }
}

Note

The API token is only returned once when created. Make sure to copy it and store it securely.

docs.title: List API Tokens
docs.text:
This path returns the list of API tokens for the authenticated user.

Method Path GET /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "Xl2yU1rcy2BP",
                "name": "My Token",
                "expires_at": "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Delete an API Token
docs.text:
This path deletes an API token for the authenticated user.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens/{id}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "API token deleted successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: List a User's API Tokens (Admin)
docs.text:
This path returns a paginated list of API tokens belonging to the specified user. Requires admin privileges.

Method Path GET /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "Xl2yU1rcy2BP",
                "name": "CI Pipeline",
                "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}

docs.title: Create an API Token for a User (Admin)
docs.text:
This path creates a new API token for the specified user, as Create an API Token does for the authenticated user. Requires admin privileges.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• name (string): The name of the API token (3–50 characters).
  • expires_at (string, optional): The expiration date of the API token in RFC 3339 format. If not provided, the token will never expire.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellacore_Ab3cD4eFgHiJ_9x8wVuTsRqPoNmLkJiHgFeDcBa"
    }
}

Note

The API token is only returned once when created. Make sure to copy it and store it securely.

docs.title: Delete a User's API Token (Admin)
docs.text:
This path deletes an API token belonging to the specified user. Requires admin privileges.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens/{id}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "API token deleted successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: v1.0
docs.text:
• Release date: January 12, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.0.0

Ella Core is a simple, reliable and secure core network for private 5G deployment.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Deploy on generic hardware (amd64 or arm64)
  • Consumes very little resources
  • Packaged as 1 binary
  • Install in 5 minutes using the snap, container image or from source
  • Operate using a simple and intuitive modern UI
  • Automate tasks with a complete RESTful API and Go client
  • Validated with multiple device vendors (iOS, Android)
  • Connect up to 1000 subscribers
  • User Plane built with eBPF
  • Achieve bitrates over 10Gbps
  • Use private IP subnets with Network Address Translation (NAT) support
  • Distributed as Free and Open Source Software (Apache 2.0)
  • State-of-the-art documentation

docs.title: v1.1
docs.text:
• Release date: January 22, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.1.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Profiling API endpoints (pprof): Exposed pprof endpoints to help operators and developers analyze performance and troubleshoot CPU and memory issues.
  • Backup & restore support in Go API client: Added new functions to allow automating backup & restore using the Go client.
  • Improved primary UI dashboard: The primary dashboard has been refined for better usability and visibility into system status.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Added TRex performance test results
  • Added Baicells and Vankom to the list of supported commercial radios
  • Included links to YouTube and other social channels

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Expanded unit testing coverage:
    • Bootstrapped unit testing suite for UE-specific NGAP messages
    • Increased coverage of edge-cases in API testing suite
  • Bug fixes and security improvements
  • Dependency updates

docs.title: v1.10
docs.text:
• Release date: April 30, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.10.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text: • High Availability: Deploy Ella Core as a highly available cluster. Deploy three or Five nodes. Each node is active and can accept 5G radios and subscriber traffic. Raft is used as the consensus algorithm between nodes. Persistent resources (subscribers, policies, operator info) are replicated across the cluster and runtime state (Radio connections, PDU sessions, user plane state) is tied to individual nodes.

docs.title: v1.11
docs.text:
• Release date: May 20, 2026

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• End-to-end IPv6 support: Deploy Ella Core on IPv6 hosts, provision subscribers with IPv6 addresses, advertise those addresses to IPv6 BGP peers, create IPv6 network rules, and monitor IPv6 traffic flows.
  • Claude AI agent marketplace plugin: Install the Ella Core AI skill via the Claude marketplace plugin. This makes it easier and faster to manage your private 5G network with AI agents.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Integration tests overhaul: As we write more code with AI, the change velocity increases and we get less good at reviewing code. To balance the problem and maintain a high level of reliability through changes, we significantly increase integration test coverage. Our integration tests now completely cover the API, HA and network rules. Future releases will continue expanding this support. Read more about this idea here.
  • Complete Go client: Manage network interfaces, flow accounting and BGP via to Go client SDK. You can now use the Go client to perform every API action.

docs.title: v1.12
docs.text:
• Release date: June 18, 2026

  • GitHub release: v1.12.0

  • Update the license to Business Source (BUSL-1.1): If you use Ella Core in production, you will need to purchase a Production License from us. If you run Ella Core in non-production environments you can continue using it for free. Our intent is for Ella Networks to be commercially sustainable over the long run and keep on shipping awesome features to a wide range of organization. Read the license FAQ for more details.

docs.title: v1.13
docs.text:
• Release date: July 10, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.13.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• 4G support: Run a 4G and 5G private network with Ella Core, still a single, lightweight binary. 5G radios still connect to Ella Core's n2 interface on port 38412 and 4G radios can now connect on port 36412. 4G has been validated with multiple devices (iPhone, Samsung, and more), the list will grow over the next few months. 4G and 5G are on by default. Admins can manage 4G and 5G access via subscriber profiles. Many items in the UI have been made neutral to accommodate both 4G and 5G versions.
  • Location support (beta): Beta APIs for tracking subscriber location via Cell ID or Enhanced Cell ID (E-CID). This feature is not yet available via the UI.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:

docs.title: v1.14
docs.text:
• Release date: July 21, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.14.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Framed Routing: Allow an IP network to sit behind a UE so that a range of IP addresses is reachable over a single PDU session. Administrators can manage framed routes via the data networks page in the UI or the API.
  • Static IPs: Assign specific IP addresses to your mobile subscribers. Administrators can manage static IPs via the data networks page in the UI or the API. Static IPs are optional, dynamic allocation remains the default IP allocation mechanism.
  • Location on 4G (beta): The location beta (Cell ID and E-CID) now supports 4G subscribers in addition to 5G.
  • Location with A-GNSS (beta): Extends the location beta with Assisted GNSS (A-GNSS) positioning via the LTE Positioning Protocol (LPP), building on the Cell ID and E-CID support introduced in v1.13. This feature is only available for 5G subscribers at the moment and requires device support.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:

docs.title: v1.15
docs.text:
• Release date: July 28, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.15.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Direction-aware NAT: NAT connection tracking now records the direction a flow was initiated in, so only downlink traffic that belongs to a connection opened by a subscriber is forwarded. Unsolicited packets from the data network are dropped at the NAT boundary. The NAT port range was also moved outside the host's ephemeral range to avoid collisions with host-initiated traffic.
  • Unified eBPF datapath: The eBPF program was simplified and consumes less memory.
  • Location (beta): Stale Cell ID locations are now automatically refreshed.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:

  • Bug fixes

docs.title: v1.16
docs.text:
• Release date: August 24, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.16.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• eBPF TCX user plane: Attach Ella Core's user plane program to the TCX hook. TCX allows Ella Core to work on every modern Linux system, regardless of driver support. It replaces XDP Generic as a fast and reliable fallback option on systems without XDP Native support. XDP Native remains the preferred option when possible. XDP Generic should only be used for test and dev deployments.
  • 4G <-> 5G Interworking: Subscribers can smoothly transition from 4G to 5G and vice-versa via N26 (and non-n26) handover, maintaining their IP session.
  • Local switching: Allow direct UE-to-UE (hairpin) communication. This feature is disabled by default and can be enabled via the UI in the Networking page or the API.
  • IP Fragments: Support IPv4 and IPv6 fragments in subscriber data path.
  • NITZ: Send network time to UEs.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Use in-house S1AP, NGAP, NAS, and PER libraries.
  • Add Baicells Neutrino 220 to supported 4G radios
  • Add Playwright UI end-to-end tests

docs.title: v1.17
docs.text:
• Release date: September 3, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.17.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Subscriber discoverability: Write a short description to easily differentiate subscribers (ex. "campsite 1", "camera1-venue2"). Search subscribers by IMSI or description.
  • Subscriber Connection state: View the subscriber's connection state ("Connected" or "Idle"). View the last radio the subscriber was connected to, even when the subscriber goes Idle.
  • Radio Status: View the radio status ("Online" or "Offline"). Radios now remain visible to users when they go offline. Users can manually "Forget" offline radios.
  • Decode all radio events: Every S1AP, NGAP and NAS message Ella Core sends or receives is now visible in the network event decoder.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Add Google Pixel 10a to supported devices
  • Trim container image and snap size by >30%
