docs.title: v1.18
docs.text:
Breaking changes

This release contains breaking changes. Review the Breaking changes section below before upgrading. For clusters, follow the upgrade guide.

  • Release date: September 16, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.18.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Downlink buffering for idle subscribers: Downlink packets addressed to an idle subscriber are now buffered while Ella Core pages it, and sent to the subscriber once the session is re-established.
  • Handover data forwarding: Subscribers keep their traffic through 4G and 5G handovers. Ella Core now supports both direct and indirect forwarding, and sends GTP-U End Markers on the old tunnel.
  • Subscriber registrations: The subscriber API exposes the RAN and core UE identities (RAN/AMF UE NGAP ID, eNB/MME UE S1AP ID). Those can be used for correlating UE events with the radios.
  • Dark mode: The UI now supports dark mode.
  • Time range picker: Network events, traffic and audit logs share a common time range picker.
  • Observability overhaul: Metrics follow Prometheus naming conventions, logs use consistent field names with less noise at info-level, and the eBPF datapath exposes more metrics, including its memory usage in the UI.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Standardize radio identity model across 4G and 5G
  • Improve co-hosting with OCUDU docs for permanent setups
  • Performance improvements
  • Security fixes
  • Bug fixes
  • Dependency updates

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
• Radios are now addressed by their ref field: GET/DELETE /api/v1/ran/radios/{ranNodeType}/{id} -> GET/DELETE /api/v1/ran/radios/{ref} (ex. gNB:001-01:00002a@24)
  • The deprecated supported TAI field was removed from the radio list endpoint.
  • On the subscriber detail endpoint, the merged status object is replaced by a registrations array, sessions[].radio_access_type becomes sessions[].system, and ciphering_algorithm and integrity_algorithm report the spec's 128- prefixed names. On the subscriber list, status.radio_access_types becomes status.systems.
  • Time filters changed format. start and end are now RFC3339 instants. /subscriber-usage records are typed objects ({"date": …} / {"imsi": …}) instead of single-key maps.
  • Metrics were renamed to follow Prometheus conventions. app_sessions_total -> app_sessions, app_ip_addresses_total -> app_ip_addresses, app_ip_addresses_allocated_total -> app_ip_addresses_allocated, and app_upf_pipeline_latency_nanoseconds_total -> app_upf_pipeline_latency_seconds_total.

If you depend directly on the API, you may need to adapt your integration.

docs.title: v1.19
docs.text:
• Release date: September 24, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.19.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Manage High Availability (HA) cluster via the UI: To form a cluster, connect to a node, click on Cluster and create a join token, then connect to another node and provide it with the token and cluster address. Nodes are identified by an automatically generated UUID and can be given a display name. The dashboard shows cluster health. You only need to interact with the config file to set up the cluster bind address.
  • VRF awareness: Ella Core detects Linux VRFs and binds to them. This allows users to completely isolate their user plane subscriber traffic from management.
  • Backup integrity: Backup archives are verified (SHA-256 digest, gzip stream and SQLite structure) before being restored.

docs.title: Deprecations
docs.text: • The cluster.node-id, cluster.peers, cluster.join-token and cluster.initial-suffrage config file options are deprecated. Use the API or UI instead.

docs.title: v1.2
docs.text:
• Release date: January 28, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.2.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• 10 new metrics: Get insight into control plane, user plane, API, and database operations. Use these metrics to create comprehensive dashboards and alert rules.
  • Grafana dashboards: Import pre-built dashboards in Grafana: "Network Health" for day-to-day private 5G operations and "Deep dive" for developers needing deep insight into Ella Core's performance.
  • Standardize logging: Standardize file and stdout logs to JSON format for better parsing and searchability in centralized logging tools like Loki and Opensearch.

docs.title: Maintenance

docs.title: v1.20
docs.text:
• Release date: October 19, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.20.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Voice: Subscribers can make voice and video calls over 4G (VoLTE) and 5G (VoNR) using an external IMS (ex. Ella IMS or Kamailio). Ella Core acts as the HSS (Cx) and PCRF/PCF (Rx) for the IMS, and carries SIP signalling and call media on a dedicated ims data network.
  • SMS: Subscribers can send and receive SMS over 4G and 5G using an external SMSC (ex. Ella SMSC). Ella Core carries messages in NAS signalling and connects to SMSCs over Diameter (SGd and S6c). Configure SMSC peers and Ella Core's SMS number from the Operator page.
  • Location (Beta):
    • Locate 4G subscribers with A-GNSS and UE-assisted E-CID over LPP.
    • Choose the E-CID measurement quantities in location requests.
    • Request periodic location reports for a subscriber.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Snap auto-connect: snap install ella-core now connects the required interfaces automatically, with no snap connect commands needed.
  • OCUDU snap: Install OCUDU with snap install ocudu. See the co-hosting guide.
  • Distributed tracing across HA nodes
  • Bug fixes
  • Dependency updates

docs.title: v1.21
docs.text:
• Release date: November 3, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.21.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT): Subscribers can make MCPTT calls over 4G and 5G using an external IMS and a 3GPP MCPTT server. See the MCPTT guide.
  • IMS Application Servers: Configure IMS application servers (ex. MCPTT, Voicemail) from the Operator page and route subscribers to them with IMS filter criteria on their profile.
  • SMS over IP: Ella Core acts as the HSS for the IMS's IP-SM-GW. While an IP-SM-GW is registered for a subscriber, incoming SMS are delivered over the IMS.
  • Distributed tracing: Follow a request end to end across Ella Core, Ella SMSC and Ella IMS, ex. an SMS from the routing lookup to delivery to the phone. Trace context is carried over Diameter with every peer, and traces are exported over OTLP to any OpenTelemetry backend (ex. Grafana Tempo, Jaeger). See the observability reference.
  • Traffic class metrics: New app_upf_session_* Prometheus metrics count forwarded packets, bytes and drops (per reason) by slice, data network and 5QI.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Support bundle now includes Ella Core logs and all configuration data.
  • Bug fixes
  • Dependency updates

docs.title: v1.22
docs.text:
Breaking changes

This release contains breaking changes. Review the Breaking changes section below before upgrading. For clusters, follow the upgrade guide.

  • Release date: November 11, 2026
  • GitHub release: v1.22.0

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
• Roaming (local breakout): Ella Core acts as a visited network for roaming partners over 4G and 5G. The subscriber's home network authenticates them and holds their subscription, and Ella Core carries their traffic to its local data networks. Configure roaming partners from the Integrations page and view roamers from the Subscribers page. See the roaming guide.
  • Integrations page: A new page to configure IMS, SMS and Roaming.
  • Multiple network instances: Each data network can leave the user plane on its own interface, VLAN or VRF. Declare network instances in the config file and pick one per slice and data network. For example, when co-hosting Ella Core with Ella IMS and Ella SMSC, the ims data network leaves through a veth into the IMS namespace while internet leaves through N6. See the co-hosting guide.
  • DSCP marking: Downlink GTP-U packets on N3/S1-U are marked with a DSCP value derived from the QoS flow's 5QI and ARP (ex. EF for voice).
  • RAN trace correlation: Ella Core sends each UE's 3GPP trace ID to the radio and uses it as the OpenTelemetry trace ID, allowing distributed tracing through the RAN and the core.
  • Kubernetes hardening: New /api/v1/livez and /api/v1/readyz health endpoints. The Kubernetes manifests no longer run Ella Core as a privileged container, and add explicit capabilities, resource limits and startup, readiness and liveness probes, in line with CNTi best practices.

  • Support bundle: Click on "Support Bundle" and generate a support bundle that contains a summary of Ella Core's configuration and data, with sensitive fields removed. Share this package with Ella Networks when you need support. You can view and edit the content of the bundle before sharing it. This feature is only available to admins.
  • User detail page: Click on a user ID and manage API tokens, edit roles and view recent audit logs. This page is only available for admins and is especially useful to provision API tokens for other users.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
This change can be breaking for some users. By adding support for multiple home network keys, Ella Core now respects the home network key ID set in the SIM card and rejects registration requests for IDs not associated with a key. If you see registration rejects with the log below, go to the operator page and make sure the ID matches with the one configured in the SIM card.

Mar 17 12:06:55 raspberrypi main[4120]: {"level":"warn","ts":"2026-03-17T12:06:55.533-0400","caller":"gmm/handle_registration_request.go:217","msg":"Authentication procedure failed, rejecting registration","component":"AMF","AMF_UE_NGAP_ID":"AMF_UE_NGAP_ID:10","error":"failed to send ue authentication request: ausf UE Authentication Authenticate Request failed: failed to create auth data: couldn't convert suci to supi: home network key not found (scheme=A, keyId=1): not found"}

API endpoints used to manage home network keys changed. If you explicitly depend on the API, adapt your script to use the new endpoints. View the Operator API documentation here.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
In these tutorials, we will learn how to deploy and operate an end-to-end mobile network with Ella Core.

Choose the tutorial that best fits your setup:

Tutorial Hardware Required Installation Method Duration Simulated 5G Network Any computer will do Docker ~10 min 5G Network with Radio Hardware Linux Host, 5G radio, UE, SIM cards Snap ~30 min

If you are new to Ella Core or don't have 5G hardware, start with the Simulated 5G Network tutorial. It uses UERANSIM to simulate a radio and user equipment, so you can experience the full end-to-end flow without any specialized hardware.

If you have a 5G radio and user equipment, the 5G Network with Radio Hardware tutorial walks you through a real-world deployment on bare metal using Snap.

docs.title: Getting Started: 5G Network with Radio Hardware
Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware)
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will deploy a complete end-to-end 5G network using Ella Core with a real 5G radio and user equipment. We will install Ella Core on bare metal using Snap, burn a SIM card, configure the network, and validate that a subscriber can connect and reach the internet.

You can expect to spend about 30 minutes completing this tutorial.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
To complete this tutorial, you will need the following:

Computer

  • A Linux machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
  • 2 network interfaces:
    • One for the radio connection (N2/N3 — control and user plane)
    • One for internet connectivity (N6 — data network) and the API/UI
  • See the full system requirements

5G Equipment

  • A compatible 5G radio
  • A compatible 5G phone

SIM Card Provisioning

  • Programmable SIM cards (e.g. Sysmocom sysmoISIM-SJA5)
  • A SIM card reader/writer (e.g. HID OmniKey 3121)
  • A SIM card programming tool (e.g. pySim) installed on your machine

docs.title: 1. Install Ella Core
docs.text:
Connect to the Linux machine where you will install Ella Core.

Install the Ella Core snap:

sudo snap install ella-core

Edit the configuration file:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml

Set the network interfaces to match your system. In this example, ens5 is connected to the radio and ens3 is connected to the internet:

/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml
logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "ens5"
    ngap-port: 38412
  n3:
    name: "ens5"
  n6:
    name: "ens3"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
datapath:
  attach-mode: "xdp-native"

Note

Replace ens5 and ens3 with the actual interface names on your machine. N2 and N3 should point to the interface connected to the radio. N6 should point to the interface connected to the internet. See the configuration reference for all available options.

Start Ella Core:

sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored

docs.title: 2. Configure a Subscriber in Ella Core
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to https://<server-ip>:5002/ to access Ella Core's UI.

You should see the Initialization page.

Create the first user with the following credentials:

  • Email: admin@ellanetworks.com
  • Password: admin

Ella Core is now initialized. You will be redirected to the dashboard.

Navigate to the Subscribers page and click on the Create button.

Create a subscriber with the following parameters:

  • IMSI: Click on the Generate button to create a random IMSI
  • Key: Click on the Generate button to create a random key
  • Sequence Number: Keep the default value
  • Profile: Keep the default value

Take note of the IMSI, Key, and OPC values. You will need them to burn the SIM card.

docs.title: 3. Burn the SIM Card
docs.text:
Insert a blank programmable SIM card into your card reader.

Use pySim to program the SIM card with the subscriber credentials from the previous step. Replace the IMSI, KEY, and OPC values below with the ones you noted:

export IMSI=<your IMSI from step 2>
export KEY=<your Key from step 2>
export OPC=<your OPC from step 2>
export MCC=001
export MNC=01
export ADMIN_CODE=<Your SIM card vendor admin code>
./pySim-prog.py -p0 -n Ella -t sysmoISIM-SJA5 -i $IMSI -c $MCC -x $MCC -y $MNC -o $OPC -k $KEY -a $ADMIN_CODE -j 1

Note

The MCC and MNC values match Ella Core's Operator configuration.

Note

The ADMIN_CODE is specific to your SIM card vendor.

Note

Some devices (e.g. iPhones) require additional SUCI configuration on the SIM card. See Managing SIM Cards for details.

Insert the programmed SIM card into your user equipment.

docs.title: 4. Connect the Radio
docs.text:
Configure your 5G radio to connect to Ella Core. You will need to set:

  • AMF Address: The IP address of your radio interface. Run ip addr show ens5 to find it (replace ens5 with your radio interface name).
  • PLMN ID: 001-01 (MCC-MNC matching Ella Core's Operator configuration)
  • TAC: 000001 (TAC matching Ella Core's Operator configuration)
  • SST/SD: 1/NULL (Slice configuration matching Ella Core's Operator configuration)

Power on the radio. For detailed instructions, see Integrate with a Radio.

In the Ella Core UI, navigate to the Radios page. You should see your radio appear as connected.

docs.title: 5. Connect the User Equipment
docs.text:
Power on the user equipment with the programmed SIM card inserted.

Set the APN to internet (matching Ella Core's default Data Network).

The device should automatically search for and connect to your network.

In the Ella Core UI, navigate to the Subscribers page. You should see that your subscriber has been assigned an IP address, confirming a successful data session establishment.

From the user equipment, try to access the internet (e.g. open a web browser and navigate to any website, or ping an external address).

Success

Congratulations! You have deployed a complete end-to-end 5G network with real hardware. Your subscriber is connected through Ella Core and can reach the internet.

docs.title: Getting Started (Simulated 5G Network)
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will deploy a complete end-to-end 5G network using Ella Core and UERANSIM (a 5G radio and user equipment simulator). By the end, a simulated subscriber will be connected to your network and able to reach the internet.

No 5G radio or specialized hardware is required.

You can expect to spend about 10 minutes completing this tutorial.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text: To complete this tutorial, you will need a Linux machine with Docker installed.

docs.title: 1. Install Ella Core and UERANSIM
docs.text:
Create a new directory for this tutorial and navigate into it:

mkdir ella
cd ella

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
services:
  ella-core:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core:v1.22.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    entrypoint: /bin/core --config /core.yaml
    privileged: true
    ports:
      - "5002:5002"
    networks:
      default:
        driver_opts:
              com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: eth0
      n3:
        driver_opts:
              com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: n3
        ipv4_address: 10.3.0.2
  ueransim:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ueransim:3.2.7
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: true
    networks:
      n3:
        driver_opts:
              com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: n3
        ipv4_address: 10.3.0.3

networks:
  n3:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 10.3.0.0/24

Start the Ella Core and UERANSIM containers:

docker compose up -d

You should see the following output:

[+] Running 4/4
 ✔ Network ella_default        Created
 ✔ Network ella_n3             Created
 ✔ Container ella-ella-core-1  Started
 ✔ Container ella-ueransim-1   Started

docs.title: 2. Initialize Ella Core
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to http://127.0.0.1:5002/ to access Ella Core's UI.

You should see the Initialization page.

Note

Your browser may display a warning about the security of the connection. You can safely ignore this warning.

Create the first user with the following credentials:

  • Email: admin@ellanetworks.com
  • Password: admin

Ella Core is now initialized. You will be redirected to the dashboard.

docs.title: 3. Create a Subscriber
docs.text:
Navigate to the Subscribers page and click on the Create button.

Create a subscriber with the following parameters:

  • IMSI: 001019756139935
  • Key: 0eefb0893e6f1c2855a3a244c6db1277
  • Sequence Number: Keep the default value.
  • OPC: Select "Provide custom OPC" and set the value to 98da19bbc55e2a5b53857d10557b1d26.
  • Profile: Keep the default value.

docs.title: 4. Connect the 5G Radio Simulator
docs.text:
Go back to your terminal, in the same directory where you created the docker-compose.yaml file.

Start the 5G radio simulator:

docker compose exec -ti ueransim bin/nr-gnb --config /gnb.yaml

You should see the following output:

UERANSIM v3.2.7
[2025-10-24 17:46:43.402] [sctp] [info] Trying to establish SCTP connection... (10.3.0.2:38412)
[2025-10-24 17:46:43.404] [sctp] [info] SCTP connection established (10.3.0.2:38412)
[2025-10-24 17:46:43.404] [sctp] [debug] SCTP association setup ascId[281]
[2025-10-24 17:46:43.404] [ngap] [debug] Sending NG Setup Request
[2025-10-24 17:46:43.405] [ngap] [debug] NG Setup Response received
[2025-10-24 17:46:43.405] [ngap] [info] NG Setup procedure is successful

Leave the radio running, don't close the terminal.

In your browser, navigate to the Ella Core UI and click on the Radios tab. You should see a radio connected with the name UERANSIM-gnb-1-1-1.

docs.title: 5. Connect the User Equipment Simulator
docs.text:
Open a new terminal window in the same directory where you created the docker-compose.yaml file.

Start the UE simulator:

docker compose exec -ti ueransim bin/nr-ue --config /ue.yaml

You should see the following output:

UERANSIM v3.2.7
[2025-10-24 17:51:25.972] [nas] [info] UE switches to state [MM-DEREGISTERED/PLMN-SEARCH]
[2025-10-24 17:51:25.973] [rrc] [debug] New signal detected for cell[1], total [1] cells in coverage

The User Equipment has successfully connected to the network and has been assigned the IP address 10.45.0.1.

Leave the UE running, don't close the terminal.

docs.title: 6. Validate the Connection
docs.text:
In your browser, navigate to the Ella Core UI and click on the Subscribers tab. You should see that the subscriber you created has been assigned an IP address matching the one from the UE output.

Open a new terminal window in the same directory where you created the docker-compose.yaml file.

Ping Google's DNS server from the subscriber's interface:

docker compose exec -ti ueransim ping -I uesimtun0 8.8.8.8 -c4

You should see a successful ping:

PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8) from 10.45.0.1 uesimtun0: 56(84) bytes of data.
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=116 time=39.0 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=116 time=37.9 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=3 ttl=116 time=37.4 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=4 ttl=116 time=18.9 ms

--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss, time 3003ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 18.865/33.300/39.038/8.355 ms

Success

Congratulations! You have deployed a complete end-to-end 5G network. A simulated subscriber is connected and can reach the internet through Ella Core.

docs.title: 7. Clean Up (Optional)
docs.text:
When you are done with the tutorial, you can remove the containers and the networks:

docker compose down
